Teams fight in controlled sections, using rests and assistants when necessary rather than wasting shots in general volleys. Their reputation is less glamorous than the cavalry’s, but every army that relies on armour eventually learns why these companies are kept close to threatened fronts.
quote_en: “If it can be measured, it can be penetrated.”

role_en: Hold distant border sectors for long periods with enough infantry, scouts and fieldcraft to survive isolation.
lore_en: The Frontier Regiments are the people asked to make an empire wider than its available army. Raised and stationed along dangerous marches, they combine line drill with local scouting, field construction and the stubborn habits of soldiers who may wait weeks for reinforcement. Uniform details vary by region, but flintlocks, bayonets and practical winter gear are universal. Their prestige comes from endurance rather than parade-ground polish: a Grenzregiment may spend an entire campaign preventing a crisis that no capital ever notices.
quote_en: “The map stays imperial because someone remains at the edge.”

role_en: Build crossings and fortifications, demolish obstacles and turn small forces into positions that can survive larger ones.
lore_en: Crown Field Pioneers treat terrain as another weapon. A village becomes a redoubt, a frozen stream a road, and an intact bridge a demolition problem according to the front. Pistols and carbines share belts with saws, axes, measuring gear and charges. Commanders trust small teams to solve impossible work under fire because a single crossing, obstacle or fieldwork can decide whether an entire regiment remains in place.
quote_en: “Give us ground and an hour.”

role_en: Seize bridges, redoubts and breaches with compact assault teams built around initiative and controlled violence.
lore_en: Crown Assault Companies are small by design. Short carbines, grenades, axes, bayonets and practical cuirasses let them move quickly through terrain where a formal battalion becomes clumsy. Their officers receive broad objectives and unusually wide freedom in how to accomplish them. The best Sturmkompanien are remembered for actions that sound implausible when reduced to numbers: a gate taken by forty soldiers, a battery silenced before dawn, a bridge held long enough for an army to cross. The empire cultivates that reputation because sometimes reputation buys the first hesitation.
quote_en: “Small enough to enter. Good enough to matter.”

role_en: Enter collapsing fronts, restore local command and counterattack before defeat becomes contagious.
lore_en: Black Eagle Companies are not a permanent super-regiment. They are compact veteran formations maintained precisely for the moments when ordinary structure has begun to fail. Their soldiers are selected for calm judgement, strong NCO leadership and the ability to absorb unfamiliar survivors into a temporary fighting group. A company may arrive to find broken infantry, abandoned guns and a road full of wounded; hours later those pieces are expected to function together again. Their legend comes from turning disasters back into battles.
quote_en: “Arrive before defeat becomes a habit.”

role_en: Protect the imperial household and act as an emergency combat reserve composed almost entirely of proven veterans.
lore_en: The Double Eagle Lifeguard recruits soldiers whose records would qualify them to command elsewhere. Immaculate charcoal uniforms, silver eagle plates and high-quality carbines distinguish them visually, but prestige is secondary to competence. Guards are expected to understand security, mounted movement, close combat and battlefield command well enough to respond when a crisis reaches the imperial staff itself. Their small numbers prevent wasteful deployment. When they do enter battle, neighbouring officers know the situation has become serious enough for Kraków to risk some of its best people.
quote_en: “Every guard could lead. Their duty is to remain.”

role_en: Cross hostile territory, raid communications and return with information conventional cavalry cannot reach.
lore_en: The Vanguard Lisowczycy preserve the independence and audacity of an older Polish raiding tradition without preserving its indiscipline wholesale. They ride light, live off carefully authorised requisition and carry carbines, pistols and sabres suited to sudden violence. Small detachments disappear beyond the recognised front to observe roads, intercept couriers and disturb depots. Headquarters often gives them an objective rather than a route. The risk is obvious; the advantage is having scouts who can still think when the map stops being useful.
quote_en: “Past the frontier, orders become judgment.”

role_en: Deliver accurate mobile fire, dismount when necessary and reinforce exposed sectors faster than foot marksmen can march.
lore_en: Vistula Carbiniers are cavalrymen whose firearm skill matters more than the charge. They ride with long carbines, pistols and sabres, then dismount when terrain or range demands a steadier shot. Their best squadrons can cross a front, establish a firing line and relocate before the enemy has decided whether to answer with cavalry or infantry. They are particularly valuable along rivers and open plains, where mobility turns a small number of excellent shots into pressure across a much larger space.
quote_en: “Ride where the rifle is needed.”

class_en: Imperial Winged Hussars · Supreme Shock Cavalry
role_en: Deliver the empire’s most decisive cavalry charge against a position already judged breakable.
lore_en: The Imperial Winged Hussars are a rebuilt Polish shock tradition, not ceremonial survivors. Blackened or silver cuirasses carry restrained red-white sashes and compact steel wing frames designed for campaign use. Long lances open the charge; pistols and sabres finish it. Riders, horses and training are too costly for mass deployment, so when several banners gather, the empire is committing a weapon it normally refuses to spend.
quote_en: “When the wings gather, someone has already lost.”

role_en: Scout aggressively, exploit breaches and turn retreat into destruction before the enemy can reform.
lore_en: Crown Uhlans provide the speed that the heavier Husaria cannot waste on routine pursuit. Their lighter horses, long lances, pistols and sabres make them suited to screens, flanking movements and the violent work that begins after a line has already cracked. Officers are expected to recognise opportunities without waiting for a headquarters map to catch up. A good Uhlan regiment does not merely chase a retreating army; it finds bridges, guns and messengers that army still needs to remain an army.
quote_en: “The breach is only the beginning.”

role_en: Escort, screen and fight repeated cavalry actions across campaigns where heavier shock units cannot remain committed.
lore_en: Kraków Pancerni occupy the space between heroic charge and ordinary cavalry labour. Riders wear practical armour and carry carbines, sabres and shorter lances, allowing them to skirmish, escort convoys, reinforce flanks or dismount when terrain demands it. They rarely receive the songs written for Winged Hussars, but they remain effective after the spectacular charge has ended and the campaign still has another week to run. Their value is that commanders can ask them to do almost anything involving a horse and expect a competent answer.
quote_en: “Glory rides once. Duty keeps riding.”

role_en: Achieve decisive effects with fewer guns through superior ranging, crew discipline and target selection.
lore_en: Kraków Field Artillery embodies the empire’s preference for quality over mass. Its crews are selected for mathematics, nerve and repetition until range estimation becomes nearly instinctive. Batteries rarely attempt to imitate Napoleon’s vast concentrations. Instead they shift targets rapidly, punish exposed officers or guns and conserve ammunition until a shot is worth taking. Other armies count cannon; Habsburg-Polish commanders often ask who is serving them. Six excellent crews in the right valley can matter more than twenty mediocre pieces firing everywhere.
quote_en: “Fewer guns. Fewer mistakes.”

role_en: Reduce major fortifications with heavy cannon, mortars and engineer-supported siege systems.
lore_en: Vienna’s siege artillery is the arm the empire commits when patience has ended. Massive guns, mortars, reinforced carriages and specialised engineers travel slowly and consume obscene amounts of powder, transport and labour. That cost is accepted because their crews are expected to solve fortresses rather than merely bombard them. Surveying, trench work and deliberate target reduction accompany every battery. Their arrival is therefore political as well as military: a government willing to haul Vienna’s heavy park across a continent has already decided the objective is worth finishing.
quote_en: “A wall is only a schedule written in stone.”

role_en: Support cavalry wings with fast batteries that relocate constantly and fire at the exact moment a manoeuvre needs weight.
lore_en: Vistula Horse Artillery follows the Polish cavalry tradition in spirit: speed matters only if it arrives with purpose. Light guns, mounted crews and excellent horse handling allow batteries to keep pace with Uhlans and Pancerni, then unlimber on ground ordinary artillery has not yet reached. They do not compete with France through sheer volume. Their crews are expected to place a handful of rounds where a charge, withdrawal or flank action will change because of them, then move before retaliation settles.
quote_en: “The shot must arrive with the horse.”

role_en: Identify, contain and destroy Vestigium threats, revenants and anomalous targets beyond conventional military expertise.
lore_en: Imperial Relic Hunters combine marksmanship, field scholarship and the unpleasant experience of surviving things that should not have been understood the first time. Their equipment includes specialised rifles, containment cases, probes, restraints and cutting tools alongside ordinary campaign kit. They are not priests and do not claim supernatural authority. Their advantage is procedural courage: approach the anomaly, learn what actually harms it, and communicate that answer before more people die. Reliktjäger detachments are small because the empire values expertise more than spectacle.
quote_en: “Courage begins after the first explanation fails.”

role_en: Keep elite weapons, armour, artillery and Vestigium equipment functioning far from ideal workshops.
lore_en: The empire’s quality would collapse quickly without people capable of preserving it. Zeugmeister are master armourers, gunsmiths and artificers assigned to field formations that cannot simply discard damaged specialist equipment. They carry precision tools, spare lockwork, armour plates and diagnostic instruments, often protected by a carbine or pistol because their workshops sit close to danger. A repaired rifle, rebalanced cuirass or functioning gun carriage can return an exceptional soldier to the line instead of turning him into an expensive casualty.
quote_en: “Excellence is useless if it breaks only once.”

class_en: Crisis Command Cadre · Imperial Field Masters
role_en: Take command of broken sectors and rebuild surviving troops, guns and supplies into a functioning force.
lore_en: The Feldmeisterkorps exists because Habsburg-Poland fights too many fronts with too few people. Its officers and senior NCOs are chosen for the ability to understand unfamiliar formations quickly and command without their own regiment. A Feldmeister may arrive with only papers, a horse and authority, then rebuild survivors, guns and supplies into a functioning force. Their victories often begin inside somebody else’s disaster.
quote_en: “Give me what survived.”

role_en: Shield coastal escorts and engage raiders without committing an oversized battlefleet.
lore_en: A conventional medium frigate receives iron protection around its lower battery and machinery spaces. One auxiliary boiler drives a screw for harbour work and emergency movement, while sail remains the cruising system. Armour adds resilience but also draft; captains depend on nearby engineering stores and refuse long unsupported chases.
quote_en: “Engineering must survive the voyage.”

role_en: Defend major crossings with a shallow-draft heavy bow gun.
lore_en: The Vistula gunboat places one substantial cannon on a reinforced central bed rather than loading a river hull with a full broadside. A small sheltered boiler powers side wheels for movement against the current. Limited bow plating protects the gun station. Narrow waterways suit its concentrated fire, while floating debris and damaged paddle housings can leave it dependent on towing.
quote_en: “The crossing has a keeper.”

role_en: Escort coastal supply traffic and drive off small privateers.
lore_en: A narrow stern and economical rig preserve the pink’s Baltic working character. Modest side guns cover merchantmen while reinforced frames tolerate hard coastal service. Artificers favour accessible fittings over ornament or experimental engines. Sail propulsion keeps the ship independent of coal; limited shot and a small crew require convoy captains to avoid prolonged duels with major frigates.
quote_en: “Hold the road across the water.”

role_en: Move bridge sections and engineering stores under protection at river crossings.
lore_en: A broad flat-bottomed hull carries dismantled pontoons, cable drums and timber instead of a heavy fighting battery. Two light guns guard unloading ramps, and sweeps keep it useful without dedicated fuel. Its strongest defence is the infantry and gunboat escort arranged before crossing work begins. A damaged ramp or shifting load can delay an entire field army.
quote_en: “The army crosses after the timber.”

role_en: Repair damaged guns and propulsion fittings near the operating squadron.
lore_en: A small armed tender turns its hold into a covered machine shop with a light forge, lifting tackle and replaceable bench tools. Its boiler serves pumps and workshop machinery rather than continuous propulsion. Sailing range lets it accompany coastal deployments, but repairs needing a full dock remain beyond it. Admirals protect the tender because five sound ships matter more than one impressive wreck.
quote_en: “Bring back a ship that can sail again.”

role_en: Fill the line, absorb losses and hold space through numbers rather than individual quality.
lore_en: Opolcheniye recruits are the cheapest human material Novgorod can turn into a battlefield formation. Their coats, muskets and training vary, but even poor recruits are accustomed to cold that would incapacitate soldiers from warmer countries. They exist to deepen a front, occupy secondary ground and buy time for artillery, machines and better troops. Nobody mistakes them for good infantry. The danger is that Novgorod can replace a ruined levy line faster than many enemies can replace the ammunition spent destroying it.
quote_en: “The north always has another line.”

role_en: Provide the main formal gun line of Novgorod’s field armies.
lore_en: Lineynaya Pekhota are the standard soldiers behind Novgorod’s reputation for mass warfare. They are adequately drilled, uniformly supplied and easy to replace, but rarely exceptional. Their strength lies in remaining functional in snow, mud and bitter cold while delivering enough musket fire to anchor the stranger weapons around them. A single battalion may disappoint an elite opponent. Ten battalions supported by frost ammunition, artillery and machines become a different problem entirely.
quote_en: “Ordinary men. Extraordinary quantities.”

role_en: Slow enemy advances and disrupt formation movement with freezing ammunition.
lore_en: Moroznye Strelki carry cartridges designed to spread intense cold through the point of impact. A hit may not kill more reliably than ordinary shot, but ice forming across joints, leather, exposed skin and weapon mechanisms steadily ruins an enemy’s ability to move and fight at normal tempo. Entire volleys can turn a charge into a stumbling advance. Novgorod values them less as killers than as battlefield manipulators: once an enemy has been slowed, something heavier is usually already coming.
quote_en: “The first bullet wounds. The cold finishes the argument.”

role_en: Close with slowed enemies and finish disrupted formations using freezing melee weapons.
lore_en: The Frost Axe troops occupy the ugly space between common infantry and true elite assault units. Their axes, sabres and heavy chopping weapons use frost-treated edges that spread numbness and ice across armour or flesh during repeated contact. Training is aggressive rather than refined, and discipline varies widely between battalions. Against a fresh formation they can be wasteful. Against troops already slowed by frost shot or artillery, they become brutally efficient.
quote_en: “Slow them first. Then make the cold personal.”

role_en: Hold trenches, redoubts and frozen chokepoints under conditions that exhaust other armies.
lore_en: The so-called Vodka Trench Guard earned its nickname through field ration culture rather than ceremonial doctrine. These soldiers specialise in miserable defensive work: frozen earthworks, half-buried gun pits, supply-starved redoubts and positions that may not see relief for days. Their equipment is ugly, layered and practical, their discipline strongest when the order is simply to remain. Alcohol rations, heavy winter clothing and generations of improvised cold-weather habits make them notoriously hard to dislodge once they have dug in.
quote_en: “Dig deep enough and winter joins your regiment.”

class_en: Elite Heavy Infantry · White Bear Guard
role_en: Serve as Novgorod’s premier heavy infantry and impose decision after mass troops and machines have prepared the field.
lore_en: The White Bear Guard proves Novgorod is not defined only by mass and eccentric machinery. Its soldiers are selected, disciplined and equipped far above the ordinary line, with reinforced winter armour, carefully maintained frost-modified muskets and elite blades. They enter where a position must be taken, a counterattack broken or an exhausted enemy finished. The rest of the army creates conditions; the Guard turns those conditions into victory.
quote_en: “The north sends thousands. Then it sends us.”

role_en: Scout, screen and shadow enemy movement while refusing decisive engagement.
lore_en: Cossack Razvedchiki are useful because they rarely fight the battle an enemy wants. They ride light, carry carbines, pistols and sabres, and spend more time observing, baiting and disappearing than attempting decisive kills. Their shooting is notoriously inconsistent, yet their information, speed and ability to stay just outside retaliation make them exhausting opponents. A commander who ignores them risks ambush. A commander who chases them usually discovers that the real Novgorod army has moved somewhere else.
quote_en: “Miss the shot. Learn the road.”

name_native: COSSACK REITERS OF THE STEPPE LINE
role_en: Raid supply lines, pressure flanks and force enemy formations to waste attention on mobile threats.
lore_en: Steppe-line Reiters carry enough firearms to remain irritating and enough mobility to avoid proving how inaccurate those firearms can be. They attack wagons, couriers, isolated gun crews and exposed flanks, then retreat before heavier cavalry can pin them. Their value is cumulative. Every escort detached to chase them weakens another column; every delayed convoy makes another battalion hungry. Novgorod uses them to make an enemy spend good troops solving bad problems.
quote_en: “A bad shot can still ruin a good march.”

role_en: Exploit broken formations and turn retreat into sustained collapse.
lore_en: Wolf Lancers are not built to charge disciplined infantry from the front. Their moment comes after frost, artillery, machines or ordinary attrition has already damaged cohesion. Light horses and long lances let them reach fugitives, exposed artillery and retreat routes before heavier cavalry could organise. They are dangerous because they understand weakness quickly. If forced to remain in a prolonged stand-up fight, their disadvantages become equally obvious.
quote_en: “We do not break the line. We chase what leaves it.”

class_en: Mobile Light Artillery · Ice Sled Battery
role_en: Move light guns rapidly across frozen ground and support fronts that ordinary wheeled artillery cannot reach.
lore_en: Ledokhod batteries turn winter terrain into an advantage. Their light guns ride on reinforced sled carriages that can cross snow and hard ice faster than conventional artillery. The price is fragility: crews are exposed, the pieces are light and broken ground quickly limits them. Novgorod accepts the trade because a gun appearing where everyone else considered movement impossible can matter more than a heavier battery arriving too late.
quote_en: “Wheels stop. The sled keeps moving.”

role_en: Bombard areas with freezing shells that disrupt movement, morale and formation cohesion.
lore_en: Moroz Mortars fire shells designed to burst into freezing fragments and clouds of supercooled residue. Their purpose is less precise destruction than battlefield disruption. Roads become slick, exposed mechanisms seize and dense formations discover that every movement takes longer than planned. The effect is temporary and uneven, but Novgorod rarely needs permanence. It needs enough delay for another line, another machine or another battery to arrive.
quote_en: “Make the ground refuse them.”

role_en: Provide crude armoured support and shock presence for mass infantry advances.
lore_en: Parovik-I is the simplest expression of Novgorod’s steam-armour doctrine: riveted plating, a compact boiler, one primary gun and enough traction to force its way through soft obstacles. It is noisy, cramped and mechanically temperamental, yet cheap enough to manufacture in useful numbers. Against ordinary infantry its presence is intimidating out of proportion to its durability. Novgorod treats losses as a production problem. If one breaks, the factory is expected to send another.
quote_en: “It only has to work longer than the attack.”

role_en: Deliver heavier short-duration fire during assaults where mobility matters more than mechanical longevity.
lore_en: The second Parovik pattern adds a second primary barrel and the mechanisms needed to service both under pressure. Firepower rises immediately; reliability does not. Crews joke that the machine contains twice the gun and three times the argument. In short assaults it can dominate a street, breach or narrow sector before defenders adjust. In prolonged operations its weight, heat and maintenance demands become increasingly obvious.
quote_en: “Two barrels. One very brief solution.”

role_en: Act as Novgorod’s most excessive armoured line breaker and psychological shock machine.
lore_en: The Tsar Pushka pattern is what happens when Novgorod answers a reasonable engineering question with an unreasonable amount of steel. Three heavy barrels dominate a reinforced steam chassis already burdened by armour, ammunition and an enormous boiler system. When everything functions at once, the machine can overwhelm a defended frontage with astonishing speed. When something fails, the repair crew learns exactly how ambitious the design was. Few units better express Novgorod’s industrial personality: crude, spectacular and willing to trade elegance for output.
quote_en: “If one gun is enough, three are convincing.”

role_en: Control trained polar bears for transport, intimidation, tracking and limited battlefield shock.
lore_en: The Bear Handlers are what keep Novgorod’s most famous animals from becoming a liability to their own army. They train, feed, harness and direct polar bears for tasks ranging from hauling heavy loads through snow to forcing light defensive positions to give way. Handlers carry firearms, control poles, chains and specialised signals according to the animal’s training. The corps treats the bear as military equipment with instincts rather than folklore. That professionalism is what makes the concept useful.
quote_en: “The bear is not the weapon until someone can aim it.”

class_en: Polar Bear Assault Corps · Monstrous Shock
role_en: Smash infantry formations and spread panic through direct organised bear assault.
lore_en: White Bear Assault formations are trained for one purpose: create a physical and psychological rupture large enough for human troops to exploit. Heavy harnesses protect vulnerable areas without sacrificing the speed and mass that make a charging polar bear terrifying. They are released in controlled groups against infantry, barricades and exposed gun crews, often after frost fire has already slowed the target. Bears can still be stopped and control can still fail, but very few soldiers remain calm when several armoured white shapes begin closing through smoke.
quote_en: “Some lines break before the claws arrive.”

role_en: Intimidate hostile fleets with enormous guns while avoiding a sustained engagement.
lore_en: A vast armoured hull carries paired monster cannon above oversized boiler rooms. The spectacle resembles a perfected steam tank afloat, but gun beds transmit recoil into the same framing that aligns its drive shafts. A full discharge can twist bearings, crack steam pipes and stop propulsion. Commanders prefer distant demonstrations; repeated battle fire can turn the flagship into its own sinking target.
quote_en: “The harbour believes every rumour.”

role_en: Threaten fortified anchorages with a siege battery whose machinery cannot endure its own fire.
lore_en: Ice Colossus concentrates its heaviest cannon forward and spreads steam machinery across an immense shallow hull. Armour seams conceal uneven framing, while repeated discharge opens joints around the bow. Floodwater reaches the low engine beds before crews can isolate it. Its guns promise harbour destruction; practical service demands conservative charges, towing support and more courage in the engine room than on deck.
quote_en: “The first shot is for the enemy.”

role_en: Hold the centre of Ottoman field armies with disciplined firearm drill while artillery and cavalry create the decisive opening.
lore_en: The Janissary musketeer remains the clearest expression of Ottoman military strength in 1717. Re-equipped with modern flintlocks, improved cartridge systems and better winter kit, these soldiers are trained to maintain controlled volleys under pressure rather than rely on spectacle. Their officers expect the line to keep functioning when smoke, casualties and broken terrain destroy parade-ground neatness. The empire may possess larger guns and faster cavalry, but every operational plan still assumes that the Janissaries will be present when the battlefield finally has to be held.
quote_en: “The empire moves because the line does not.”

class_en: Elite Assault Infantry · Janissary Forlorn Hope
role_en: Storm breaches, trenches, fortified gates and positions too dangerous for ordinary line infantry to enter first.
lore_en: Serdengeçtiler are volunteers and veterans sent into breaches, trenches and fortified gates before safe conditions exist. Grenades, short firearms, axes and heavy sidearms make them lethal in cramped assaults. Their reputation for suicidal courage hides a harder truth: the best companies know exactly how much violence is needed to open a position without becoming trapped inside it. Commanders use them sparingly because experienced assault troops are harder to replace than ammunition.
quote_en: “Open the gate. Count us afterward.”

role_en: Remove officers, gun crews and exposed specialists before the main Ottoman line reaches decisive range.
lore_en: Janissary marksmen are chosen from soldiers who combine patience with unusually consistent shooting. Their long firearms are carefully fitted and issued with better sights, powder and ammunition than common line weapons. They work ahead of the main formation or from prepared firing positions, concentrating on officers, artillery crews, messengers and anyone visibly handling Vestigium equipment. Ottoman doctrine does not romanticise the lone sniper. Nişancılar operate in small disciplined teams whose success is measured by how much easier the next infantry or artillery action becomes.
quote_en: “Remove the hand before the weapon can move.”

role_en: Expand Ottoman firepower with professional infantry that can reinforce Janissaries without copying their institutional role.
lore_en: Sekban regiments give the empire professional firearm infantry outside the Janissary establishment. Less prestigious but highly practical, they use modern muskets, reliable winter clothing and straightforward campaign drill. Provincial commanders employ them to garrison towns, reinforce threatened fronts and absorb recruits without overloading elite institutions. Quality varies between regiments, yet the best Sekban remain among the Ottoman army’s most efficient conventional soldiers.
quote_en: “The empire has more than one good line.”

role_en: Anchor critical positions with heavily protected infantry shaped by the empire’s Himyarite military inheritance.
lore_en: The Himyar Guard preserves the southern half of the empire’s military identity. Their armour, shields and decorative geometry recall older Arabian traditions, while firearms, drill and logistics are fully Ottoman. Heavy protection and disciplined close-range fire make them ideal around artillery parks, standards, command posts and narrow approaches. Foreign observers may see an archaic silhouette, but the first volley reveals how deliberately old forms have been rebuilt around modern weapons.
quote_en: “Old forms survive when they still kill.”

role_en: Keep Ottoman firearms, armour, ammunition and specialist equipment functioning across long campaigns.
lore_en: The Cebeci are one reason Ottoman elite formations can remain elite after weeks of marching and firing. Armourers, gunsmiths and ammunition specialists travel with field armies carrying spare locks, barrels, tools, cartridge materials and replacement fittings. Their work is especially important because Ottoman strength comes from conventional weapons maintained at exceptional scale rather than widespread Vestigium systems. A broken firearm is expected to return to service, not become battlefield debris. Cebeci detachments therefore sit close behind the fighting line, where repair, resupply and inspection happen continuously.
quote_en: “A weapon is only elite if it fires tomorrow.”

role_en: Undermine walls, prepare breaches and destroy fortified positions through disciplined siege engineering.
lore_en: Lağımcı sappers specialise in the patient violence required to defeat walls from beneath or within. They dig approach works, place mines, prepare demolitions and clear obstacles for assault troops under conditions where ordinary infantry would only waste lives. Their methods combine traditional Ottoman siege craft with improved explosives, surveying tools and modern field engineering. They are slow compared with cavalry and unspectacular beside giant guns, yet many Ottoman victories begin with a tunnel, a measured charge and a section of fortification collapsing exactly where the Serdengeçtiler were waiting.
quote_en: “Every wall has a lower side.”

role_en: Operate across arid, mountainous and supply-poor regions where conventional Ottoman formations lose tempo.
lore_en: Himyar desert riflemen combine southern fieldcraft with the empire’s modern firearm system. Layered clothing, strict water discipline and light equipment support long movement across arid terrain. Small detachments can screen columns, hold high ground and protect artillery routes without the supply burden of a Janissary regiment. Their rifles and drill are Ottoman; their route knowledge, camp discipline and survival habits come from the Himyarite side of the state.
quote_en: “Where the road ends, discipline keeps walking.”

role_en: Protect the imperial household and serve as a disciplined emergency reserve when ordinary formations fail near the centre.
lore_en: The Bostancı Guard occupies the boundary between palace service and battlefield responsibility. Chosen for loyalty, physical standards and composure, its companies protect imperial residences, arsenals, senior commanders and politically sensitive positions. In war they can be committed as a reserve when a breach threatens the command structure itself. They are well equipped but deliberately conventional, reflecting the Ottoman preference to trust elite people before uncertain Vestigium systems. Their prestige comes from proximity to power; their value comes from being useful when that proximity becomes dangerous.
quote_en: “Near the throne, failure travels quickly.”

class_en: Heavy Shock Infantry · Anti-Roman Monster Slayers
role_en: Break monstrous targets and hold against Western Roman forces with brutal axe work and absolute battlefield resolve.
lore_en: The Axeguard descend from formations shaped by Constantinople’s destruction. Heavy armour, reinforced axes and enough firearm support to reach melee alive are simple beside Ottoman artillery or Janissary drill, but their defining quality is hatred refined into discipline. They hold against Western Roman troops even when the enemy is undead or visibly inhuman. Years around the ruins also taught them where unnatural bodies fail under steel, making them a compact anti-monster reserve.
quote_en: “Rome took the city. It never took the men.”

role_en: Deliver disciplined shock charges against weakened lines, exposed artillery and enemy cavalry at decisive moments.
lore_en: Kapıkulu Sipahis represent the court’s professional heavy cavalry tradition after adaptation to a firearm battlefield. Armour, lance and sabre remain important, but pistols and carbines ensure they are not helpless while waiting for the moment to close. Their commanders are expected to resist premature charges and preserve the formation until artillery or infantry has created a genuine weakness. When released, they strike quickly and with enough discipline to disengage before becoming trapped in prolonged gunfire. Prestige survives here because restraint has become part of cavalry skill.
quote_en: “Ride only when the battle is ready to be broken.”

role_en: Disrupt enemy morale and exposed flanks through violent, theatrical cavalry attacks and aggressive pursuit.
lore_en: The Deliler cultivate fear as deliberately as other units cultivate accuracy. Feathers, animal skins, trophies and deliberately unsettling equipment make them visible long before contact, but the spectacle hides experienced riders who understand shock, pursuit and sudden withdrawal. Ottoman officers use them where hesitation matters: against nervous levies, disrupted lines and troops already exhausted by artillery. They are less useful in a disciplined frontal fight and can suffer badly if pinned under sustained fire. Their real weapon is the second before an enemy decides whether to stand.
quote_en: “Fear arrives before the horse.”

role_en: Provide elite Egyptian shock cavalry able to fight independently or reinforce Ottoman mounted wings.
lore_en: Egypt’s incorporation into the Ottoman war system redirected rather than erased the Mamluk military class. These riders retain exceptional horsemanship, armour traditions and personal weapon mastery inside a larger imperial command structure. Lance, sabre, pistol and carbine let them fight with unusual independence, especially in broken terrain where rigid cavalry loses coherence. Ottoman commanders value them as elite shock cavalry whose Egyptian identity survived conquest without becoming politically separate.
quote_en: “Egypt still rides. Now it rides with the empire.”

role_en: Harass flanks, screen advances and deliver mobile firearm pressure without surrendering Mamluk cavalry mobility.
lore_en: Mamluk carbine cavalry developed from the practical need to keep elite horsemen useful before the decisive charge. Riders carry compact carbines and pistols, moving in loose groups that can punish exposed infantry, scouts and artillery crews without immediately committing to melee. Their shooting is not intended to replace the musket line. It creates disorder, forces formations to turn and makes enemy cavalry reveal itself. Once the battlefield becomes uneven, the same riders can close with sabres and exploit the confusion they helped create.
quote_en: “Make them turn before you make them run.”

class_en: Blessed Heavy Cavalry · Vlad’s Last Order
role_en: Use superhuman strength, night fighting and psychological shock to destroy elite targets without surrendering human discipline.
lore_en: These are the surviving knights of Vlad’s Wallachia, still human despite the blessing left in their blood. Strength, endurance, sharpened senses and unnatural ease in darkness did not turn them into beasts. They eat, sleep, pray, obey orders and die like men. At night they move with disturbing certainty, emerging from darkness before ordinary eyes adjust. Ottoman commanders therefore treat them as rare allied cavalry, not monsters.
quote_en: “Their lord is dead. The blessing still rides.”

role_en: Provide reliable, well-drilled artillery support to Ottoman field armies across ordinary campaign conditions.
lore_en: The Topçu corps is the foundation beneath the empire’s reputation for enormous guns. Most Ottoman artillery pieces are not monsters; they are well-served field cannon crewed by professionals who understand ranging, ammunition discipline and rapid emplacement. Standardised carriages and strong logistical support allow batteries to keep pace with a large army better than foreign observers expect. Their crews rarely depend on Vestigium enhancement. Precision comes from training, tables, survey work and powder quality, proving that conventional artillery can remain strategically dominant when enough institutional knowledge supports it.
quote_en: “Before the giant cannon comes the gun that never misses its day.”

role_en: Break protected positions and crowded defences with grenades, mortars and steep-angle explosive fire.
lore_en: Humbaracı units specialise in putting explosives where direct-fire cannon cannot easily reach. Light mortars, hand-thrown grenades and compact bombard systems let them attack trenches, rooftops, reverse slopes and defended streets. Their crews train obsessively in fuse timing because a powerful shell is useless if it bursts too early over friendly troops or too late beneath empty ground. In sieges they work closely with sappers and assault companies, creating the brief windows during which a breach can be crossed before defenders recover.
quote_en: “If the wall protects them, fire over the wall.”

role_en: Destroy major fortifications and massed defensive works with artillery built around overwhelming calibre rather than mobility.
lore_en: Şahi batteries answer difficult engineering problems with overwhelming calibre. Their enormous guns demand reinforced carriages, prepared roads, heavy teams and crews trained more like siege engineers than ordinary gunners. They are slow to move and expensive to feed, but once emplaced their shells can alter fortifications rather than merely damage them. The empire brings them only when a wall, gate or fortress is important enough to justify excess.
quote_en: “Some walls deserve a larger argument.”

role_en: Engage batteries, command positions and fixed targets from distances most armies consider impractical.
lore_en: The empire’s long-range batteries are specialised weapons built around unusually long barrels, carefully measured powder charges and obsessive survey work. Their rate of fire is modest and relocation is difficult, but their purpose is not volume. They begin a battle before enemy artillery expects to be threatened, forcing command posts and batteries to move or dig deeper. Ottoman engineers accept the cost because range changes planning itself. A target that believed distance offered safety may discover that the empire designed an entire cannon specifically to disagree.
quote_en: “Distance is only another number for the gun crew.”

role_en: Move light guns with cavalry formations and place immediate fire wherever Ottoman manoeuvre creates an opportunity.
lore_en: Sürat batteries trade calibre for time. Light cannon, mounted crews and carefully selected horses let them shift between sectors far faster than the empire’s famous heavy artillery. They ride with cavalry screens, reinforce weak flanks and occupy unexpected ground long enough to fire decisive rounds before moving again. Their crews are judged by arrival and timing, proving that speed can be as valuable to Ottoman artillery as sheer weight.
quote_en: “A smaller gun in the right minute is still the bigger weapon.”

role_en: Hunt, track and eliminate any individual or creature personally marked for death by the Sultan.
lore_en: The Hassa Avcıları possess no miraculous bloodline and depend on no Vestigium relic. They are ordinary men refined through selection, fieldcraft, marksmanship, patience and an almost unreasonable ability to study prey. They may spend weeks following one commander through a campaign or enter Roman-infested territory alone to kill something that should require an artillery battery. Ottoman records credit individual Hunters with bringing down corrupted Western Roman giants through preparation, anatomy and relentless pursuit rather than supernatural strength.
quote_en: “The Sultan named you. The rest is distance.”

role_en: Anchor the imperial battle line and overwhelm opposing wooden capital ships.
lore_en: Three batteries sit inside a deeply framed timber hull with heavy cannon kept low. Imperial arsenals supply matched spars, powder and replacement carriage parts. Gilded Ottoman sternwork marks authority without concealing working decks. It is a mature sailing weapon whose strength depends on trained crews and prepared harbours; shoals and an adverse wind can still deny its impressive firepower.
quote_en: “The sea receives the Sultan’s weight.”

role_en: Sustain line combat while manoeuvring between heavier imperial squadrons.
lore_en: The broad lower hull carries a dependable two-deck battery beneath relatively restrained upperworks. Builders favour a clean sailing run and repairable framing over excessive height. Admirals use the class where squadrons must turn together and reinforce a pressured section. Its balanced design preserves endurance, but the heaviest enemy capital ships still demand coordinated engagement.
quote_en: “Victory keeps its formation.”

role_en: Coordinate the battle fleet and transmit the Kapudan’s intent across squadrons.
lore_en: A broad quarterdeck carries signal lockers, chart tables and relay stations above a capable fighting battery. Command accommodation is kept away from powder routes, and spare signal spars remain ready after damage. Ottoman officers train messenger boats alongside flag relays. Losing the flagship need not silence every squadron, though the experienced staff aboard remains costly to replace.
quote_en: “One order, many sails.”

role_en: Hold restricted approaches with concentrated broadside fire and exceptional timber protection.
lore_en: Demirkapı places dense side batteries inside thick oak framing and protected stern galleries. Its broad hull absorbs punishment better than its speed suggests, making it useful beside coastal forts and guarded convoy routes. Admirals resist the temptation to pursue light raiders with it. The vessel’s weight is valuable only where an enemy must approach.
quote_en: “The gate opens from our side.”

role_en: Protect long coastal convoys and defeat hostile frigates away from the line.
lore_en: A long single battery and extensive provisions give Hilâl independent range without the manpower of a capital ship. Ottoman timber selection emphasises durable working structure; trained gun crews keep its smaller broadside effective. It patrols convoy approaches and answers raiders before transports scatter. Against a superior line ship, its captain must preserve distance and the wind advantage.
quote_en: “The crescent keeps the road.”

role_en: Chase fast enemies and disable their rig before they escape imperial waters.
lore_en: Reduced sternwork, lighter guns and carefully distributed stores give Şahin a clean sailing profile. Chase pieces aim at spars and steering while crews change canvas rapidly. Its captains need exact judgement of wind and sail strain; overdriving the rig can end the pursuit without an enemy shot. It wins through sustained contact rather than trading weight with capital ships.
quote_en: “Flight ends where the falcon turns.”

role_en: Find hostile fleets and maintain an observation screen beyond the main squadron.
lore_en: Burak carries a light battery, generous water stores and replacement rigging in a compact ocean-going hull. Masthead watches and courier discipline make it useful before a fleet battle begins. It follows superior ships at distance and returns clear positions, avoiding an exchange it cannot survive. Prolonged bad weather taxes a small crew more quickly than its provision capacity suggests.
quote_en: “Bring back the horizon’s warning.”

role_en: Raid isolated commerce and bring captured cargo into imperial ports.
lore_en: A sharp bow, mixed sailing rig and shallow operating draft serve independent corsair captains. Light cannon damage steering and canvas, while working boats move prize parties safely. The vessel draws on the empire’s eastern maritime connections without adopting a line-ship silhouette. Every captured merchantman removes sailors from the raider, forcing an early return when success exceeds its crew reserve.
quote_en: “The cargo changes its master.”

role_en: Attack exposed coastal flanks and close on immobilised ships without depending on wind.
lore_en: Rows of oars drive a long timber hull carrying heavy forward guns and lighter rail pieces. Lateen sails extend coastal range, while a low assault deck supports controlled boarding. Ottoman galley discipline remains valuable in narrow sheltered water. Large rowing crews and low freeboard make lengthy open-sea operations an expensive misuse of the design.
quote_en: “The oars answer when the wind falls silent.”

role_en: Lead galley squadrons and seize defended vessels in restricted water.
lore_en: The enlarged galley combines a substantial forward fighting platform with command space over the stern. Stronger benches and spare oars sustain manoeuvre through crowded approaches. Its prestige rests on coordinating close assault, not matching a sailing three-decker gun for gun. Rowers, boarders and officers require a formidable daily supply even before combat losses are considered.
quote_en: “Close together. Board together.”

role_en: Deliver concentrated forward and side fire while supporting sheltered-water assaults.
lore_en: A broad oared hull carries substantial cannon on a reinforced working deck. Short lateen masts assist movement between nearby bases, while anchors steady the vessel for bombardment. It brings more artillery than a galley but pays in acceleration and crew demand. Admirals use it beside harbour approaches where escorts can cover its slow turns.
quote_en: “Hold the water while the guns work.”

role_en: Throw mortar shells behind coastal walls from surveyed offshore positions.
lore_en: A heavily braced central well receives the mortars, with rigging displaced from their firing arcs. Separate shell stores and trained powder handlers make sustained siege work possible. The vessel anchors with an escort screen and relies on shore observers for useful correction. Its powerful high-angle weapon gives little protection against a frigate closing at speed.
quote_en: “The rampart has another side.”

role_en: Protect estuaries and local anchorages with a heavy forward gun.
lore_en: A shallow timber hull spreads one heavy barrel’s recoil along substantial longitudinal beams. Sweeps and a small lateen sail keep it mobile within protected water. Provincial arsenals can maintain its simple fittings with ordinary tools. Its limited battery cannot answer a broadside duel, and a rising offshore sea can interrupt even a carefully prepared coastal engagement.
quote_en: “The shallow water also has teeth.”

role_en: Move infantry and field equipment between secure ports and prepared landings.
lore_en: Wide hatchways, removable troop platforms and numerous service boats define this armed transport. A moderate sailing rig keeps handling manageable while stores support soldiers through the voyage. Its deck guns defend the convoy rather than make it a front-line warship. Effective landings depend on boats, shore access and escorts arriving together; crowded quarters make delay costly.
quote_en: “Carry the army to a usable shore.”

role_en: Keep dispersed squadrons supplied with powder, food and replacement naval fittings.
lore_en: Strong cargo decks separate grain, shot and powder compartments while accessible spars ride above protected hatchways. Defensive cannon and an experienced sailing crew keep the storeship from being an easy prize. It travels at convoy speed and delivers to planned anchorages. A commander who spends its cargo capacity on excessive armament starves the very fleet it exists to sustain.
quote_en: “A fleet fights what its holds can carry.”

role_en: Carry assault parties through shoal approaches and alongside defended ships.
lore_en: A compact oared hull keeps its profile low beneath harbour batteries. Hinged boarding platforms, grapnel lockers and small swivel guns support the final approach. It is a specialised vessel carrying soldiers, not a personnel entry. Surprise and a clear withdrawal route determine survival; exposed daylight attacks can destroy the boat before its platforms reach a target.
quote_en: “The harbour gate has water beneath it.”

role_en: Carry urgent orders between coastal squadrons through crowded and windless channels.
lore_en: A light mixed sail-and-oar hull uses a small crew and modest defensive guns. The design prioritises acceleration, readable signals and secure message storage. Ottoman commanders employ it where a masthead flag cannot reach another anchorage. It lacks the provision capacity for extended offshore scouting and must evade any enemy capable of forcing a close exchange.
quote_en: “An order arrives before the tide turns.”

role_en: Find routes, remove exposed leaders and mark the approach so the rest of the army can close unseen.
lore_en: Finnish White Ghosts are scouts and marksmen who turn snow, fog and broken ground into concealment. White-grey kit is cut for movement rather than parade, and their long rifles open a fight only after silence has already carried them into position. Each carries a blue Vestigium puukko whose thin luminous edge is reserved for sentries and the moment escape becomes hand-to-hand. They rarely hold ground; their value is that the enemy discovers the Danes have arrived only after someone important has already fallen.
quote_en: “You saw the shot. Never the shooter.”

role_en: Slip through screens and remove officers, gun crews, scouts and Vestigium operators before the main assault begins.
lore_en: The Blue Lynx are Finnish close hunters trained to cross the final distance without giving the enemy a clean moment to fire. Their camouflage, fieldcraft and light-bending blue Vestigium suppress outline and movement rather than making them magically absent. Carbines are used when necessary; paired cutting blades do the work once they reach command posts, batteries and rear lines. In snow, fog, forest or broken terrain, survivors often describe the same terror: nothing was visible until a blue edge was already within arm’s reach.
quote_en: “If you can see the blade, it has already passed you.”

role_en: Crash into armoured infantry and fortified melee positions with Vestigium axes built to sever protection instead of battering through it.
lore_en: Norwegian Fjord Cleavers carry the oldest visual memory in the army without becoming a reenactment of the Viking age. Heavy campaign coats, reinforced cuirasses and compact firearms get them to the fight; blue Vestigium axes finish it. Their weapons are prized for cutting cleanly through armour plates, shield rims and weapon shafts where ordinary steel would catch or deform. Fjordhoggere train for steep ground and violent short engagements, striking hard enough to open a formation before enemy firepower can recover.
quote_en: “One swing. Two pieces.”

class_en: Apex Heavy Infantry · Norse Veteran Order
role_en: Destroy elite infantry and hold the decisive melee with the finest blue-edged weapons and discipline in the northern army.
lore_en: The Blue Guard preserves the Jomsviking name as a veteran order rather than a costume from another age. Their armour is the best the kingdom can maintain, while long axes and heavy swords carry exceptionally refined blue Vestigium edges. Small, exact formations are committed against enemy elites, monsters and positions where ordinary shock troops would lose momentum. Their rarity is deliberate: the order protects a standard intended to outlive generations.
quote_en: “The old name survived because the standard did.”

role_en: Hold objectives, choke points and exposed ground when concealment fails and the army finally has to stand in plain sight.
lore_en: The Steadfast Tin Guard gives the Danish arm of the kingdom its battlefield character. Less elusive than Finnish or Swedish formations, they rely on drill, composure and refusal to yield. Muskets and controlled volleys carry them through the approach; heavy blue Vestigium sabres take over once lines close. When a pass must be held or a retreat needs one formation left behind, the Tin Guard becomes the piece that simply does not move.
quote_en: “Every man falls in place.”

role_en: Move through dense woodland without roads, control flanks and make entire enemy formations turn toward threats they cannot locate.
lore_en: Swedish Forest Shadows treat woodland as a road system visible only to themselves. Small units move through undergrowth, snow-heavy pine and broken slopes without leaving the broad tracks expected from formed infantry. Carbines and blue Vestigium blades let them harass a column, disappear and reappear along a different flank before the response is organised. Their purpose is not merely concealment. By choosing paths the enemy cannot use, Skogsskuggor decide where contact happens and which direction a formation must face when it begins.
quote_en: “The forest does not move. We do.”

class_en: Heavy Forest Infantry · Monster & Armour Hunters
role_en: Kill monsters, armoured troops and shielded formations with heavy blue-edged polearms while retaining exceptional mobility in forest terrain.
lore_en: Bluewood Hewers are the heavy answer hidden inside Sweden’s forests. Their poleaxes and great cleavers scale blue Vestigium cutting edges for thick armour, unnatural bodies and targets too large for lighter blades. Medium-heavy protection would hinder ordinary troops among roots and dense trees, but the Hewers train until that terrain becomes part of their footwork. Forest Shadows find the target; the greatblades finish the hunt.
quote_en: “The forest marks the path. We cut the rest.”

role_en: Protect commanders and decisive ground with heavily armoured household infantry built to absorb the violence of close battle.
lore_en: The Royal Huscarls are the crown’s old household tradition rebuilt for the wars of 1717. Heavy mail and plate sit beneath rich fur mantles, broad shields cover the advance and brutal axes answer anything that reaches the protected line. Unlike the Jomsvikingr, whose purpose is to seek and destroy elite opposition, Huscarls are guardians first: they close around kings, standards, officers and breaches that must not widen. Their equipment is expensive, their pace deliberate and their loyalty treated as a military asset in its own right.
quote_en: “The crown stands because we do.”

role_en: Break frightened or disordered formations through violent close assault before the enemy can recover its cohesion.
lore_en: Ulfhednar carry the most savage surviving strand of Norway’s warrior culture, but their fury is trained rather than mindless. Wolf pelts, lighter armour and paired axes give them a terrifying silhouette while leaving enough freedom to sprint through broken ground and exploit a wavering line. Officers commit them when hesitation has already appeared, because an Ulfhednar charge turns fear into collapse faster than disciplined troops can repair it. They are dangerous precisely because the violence is deliberate: the warrior beneath the wolf skin still knows when to stop.
quote_en: “The howl begins after the line has already broken.”

role_en: Advance under fire, deliver disciplined close volleys and finish the engagement with bayonet and sword.
lore_en: The Karoliner are Sweden’s answer to the idea that musket infantry must win by standing still. Their blue-and-yellow ranks advance with unnerving restraint, conserving fire until distance has collapsed and the enemy’s nerves matter as much as its armour. A close volley is followed immediately by bayonet, sword and forward pressure, turning a firearm formation into an assault column in seconds. They are less elusive than Sweden’s forest troops, but when concealment is unnecessary few northern units cross open ground with greater conviction.
quote_en: “Save the powder. Spend the distance.”

role_en: Seize difficult objectives through cold, exhaustion and hostile terrain when lighter infiltrators cannot hold what they discover.
lore_en: The Sisu Vanguard gives Finland an assault arm for missions that begin where reconnaissance ends. Their equipment remains lighter than Danish heavy infantry, but reinforced coats, compact firearms and blue-edged axes or blades let them keep fighting after long approaches through snow and broken country. They are selected less for spectacle than for the ability to continue when cold, fatigue and isolation have already reduced other formations. White Ghosts find the route; the Vanguard is sent when somebody must reach the end of it and stay there.
quote_en: “Farther is not the same as impossible.”

role_en: Use rare storm Vestigium in close combat to stun armoured enemies and tear openings through elite formations.
lore_en: Thunder Warriors belong to the kingdom’s smallest and most carefully watched martial orders. Each carries an ancient or reconstructed storm relic bound into a hammer, axe or spear, allowing controlled electrical discharge through the weapon at the instant of impact. They cannot command storms like gods, and their relics demand recovery, maintenance and restraint between major releases. In battle they are committed where ordinary blue-edged steel is insufficient and a few seconds of paralysis can decide an entire melee.
quote_en: “Steel opens the armour. Thunder opens the man.”

role_en: Strike ports, camps and rear positions from coastlines and rivers before heavier formations can react.
lore_en: Nordic Coastal Raiders preserve the old northern instinct for arriving where an enemy did not prepare a front. Light armour, axes, short firearms and boarding blades let them move from longboat or warship to shore without the burden of a formed regiment. They burn stores, seize bridges, silence batteries and withdraw before a conventional response can gather. Their warfare is not nostalgic Viking theatre; it is eighteenth-century raiding discipline sharpened by generations of northern seamanship.
quote_en: “A coastline is only a wall to men without boats.”

role_en: Fight aboard warships, seize ports and hold beachheads until the main army can land and organise.
lore_en: The Royal Marines are the professional counterpart to the kingdom’s coastal raiders. Muskets, boarding axes, short sabres and compact equipment are chosen for decks, docks and narrow streets rather than long marches inland. They protect naval guns from boarding, storm harbour works and form disciplined bridgeheads for larger expeditions arriving behind them. Where Kystraidere thrive on surprise and withdrawal, Sømarines are expected to remain after the first boats have touched shore.
quote_en: “The fleet brings the army. We bring the fleet ashore.”

role_en: Scout beyond the infantry screen, exploit broken formations and pursue enemies too fast for the northern foot regiments to catch.
lore_en: Hakkapeliitta are the kingdom’s small but valuable mounted arm, drawn from Finland’s hard-riding military tradition. They carry carbines, swords and light field equipment, avoiding the weight and ceremony of continental heavy cavalry. Their horses give the Danes a means to chase a routed enemy, screen an exposed march or raid across open country where camouflage alone cannot create speed. They remain an auxiliary to an infantry-dominated army, which is exactly why opponents often forget to account for them until pursuit begins.
quote_en: “The infantry finds you. We make sure you do not leave.”

role_en: Keep pace with aggressive infantry and deliver fast, accurate fire without turning the army into a slow siege column.
lore_en: Royal Field Guns give the Danes artillery without asking them to imitate Ottoman mass or super-heavy calibre. Crews favour lighter pieces, disciplined limbers and firing positions that can be abandoned as quickly as they are prepared. Their task is to break a strongpoint, punish a visible formation and move before counter-battery fire fixes them in place. Northern commanders treat artillery as a tool for preserving infantry momentum, not as the centre around which the entire army must march.
quote_en: “Fire, limber, move. The infantry should never wait for us.”

role_en: Disrupt dense formations and Vestigium systems with rare electrical artillery built around ancient northern storm relics.
lore_en: The Thunder Battery is one of the few places where the kingdom allows mythic Vestigium to become an organised weapon system. Conventional cannon frames are rebuilt around scarce storm relics that charge specialised shot with violent electrical discharge, stunning men, frightening animals and interfering with sensitive equipment near impact. The batteries are powerful but rare, temperamental and impossible to replace at the rate ordinary guns are lost. They therefore support decisive operations rather than serving as the normal artillery arm of the kingdom.
quote_en: “The gun fires once. The sky answers twice.”

role_en: Control routes, coordinate hidden detachments and turn forests into layered ambush systems rather than isolated hiding places.
lore_en: Skogsmästare are not merely better Skogsskuggor; they are the people who decide where the shadows should be. Veteran pathfinders learn watercourses, ridges, animal tracks and winter canopy until a forest becomes a map of firing lanes, false trails and withdrawal routes. They coordinate scouts, marksmen and heavy Hewers across ground that conventional officers struggle even to describe. When a Swedish woodland defence appears to attack from several directions at once, a Forest Master has usually been arranging the battle long before the first shot.
quote_en: “A forest has roads. You were simply never shown them.”

role_en: Track and kill dangerous individuals, beasts and isolated Vestigium threats across terrain where ordinary pursuit fails.
lore_en: The Winter Hunters are Finland’s answer to targets that refuse to remain where an army can surround them. Long rifles, traps, field knives and specialised ammunition support days of pursuit through snow, forest and abandoned country with almost no external supply. Unlike White Ghosts, who shape the opening of a battle, Metsästäjät may follow one creature or fugitive until the campaign has moved far away. Their prestige comes from patience: once a Hunter accepts a trail, distance becomes the target’s problem rather than his own.
quote_en: “Run if you like. Tracks are a kind of promise.”

role_en: Shape local electrical conditions, support storm relic units and create brief battlefield windows that conventional troops can exploit.
lore_en: Stormmestre are scholars, veterans and relic-bearers capable of controlling northern storm Vestigium beyond the level of a single weapon strike. Their art can charge prepared conductors, redirect electrical discharge, veil an approach beneath violent weather or strengthen a Thunder Battery for one carefully timed salvo. Such feats are local, costly and dependent on both relic and atmosphere; no Storm Master can summon endless hurricanes on command. Their importance lies in coordination, turning several rare pieces of mythic technology into one coherent battlefield event.
quote_en: “We do not command the storm. We persuade it where to stand.”

role_en: Break the opposing battle line with a sustained, concentrated broadside.
lore_en: Four continuous gun decks rise above a heavily braced hull. Danish yards distribute ballast low and carefully balance the sail plan, allowing the giant to turn with surprising authority. Its full broadside punishes wooden opponents, while deep draught and enormous crew requirements bind it to maintained channels and major supply ports.
quote_en: “Four decks. One answer.”

role_en: Coordinate close fleet action while anchoring the strongest squadron.
lore_en: Nordkrone trades some upper-deck battery space for signal stations and sheltered command galleries. A strong four-deck hull keeps the admiral close enough to judge the line’s movement. Redundant halyards and disciplined signalling guide aggressive turns; the conspicuous flagship attracts concentrated enemy fire and needs a clear view of its escorts.
quote_en: “The fleet turns with us.”

role_en: Exploit gaps opened by the four-deck ships and protect their exposed flanks.
lore_en: A lower two-deck profile and responsive helm make Havbjørn the fleet’s turning arm. Strong knees and stout planking survive hard exchanges without imposing the giant ships’ deepest draught. Captains wheel into an enemy’s damaged line or screen a flagship’s stern. Its smaller battery requires positional advantage against heavier capital ships.
quote_en: “Where the gap opens, we enter.”

role_en: Run down hostile raiders and keep contact with retreating ships.
lore_en: Long waterlines and generous canvas give Havfalk the reach to catch prey beyond the main fleet. A single covered battery and useful chase guns support pursuit without weighing down the hull. Captains report targets before committing, then damage rigging to slow escape. Light protection makes prolonged exchanges with ships of the line costly.
quote_en: “Run. We have more sea.”

role_en: Close under oars, fasten alongside and deliver a boarding party.
lore_en: Ulvetand carries the old northern appetite for capture into a low, compact galliot. Sweeps overcome a dying breeze, grapnels secure the enemy rail and a clear waist gives boarders room to gather. Light guns cover the approach. The hull is dangerous beside an isolated opponent and vulnerable beneath a prepared broadside.
quote_en: “Keep the hull. Take the deck.”

role_en: Hold narrow coastal approaches and support attacks inside the fjords.
lore_en: Fjordvagt spreads the recoil of a heavy forward gun across a shallow, reinforced hull. A modest sail and banks of sweeps move it between surveyed anchorages. Local pilots exploit shoals that constrain larger ships. Limited stores and low freeboard keep the vessel near shelter, where a carefully chosen channel gives its gun real authority.
quote_en: “The narrow water belongs to us.”

role_en: Lob heavy shells into coastal batteries before the landing fleet closes.
lore_en: A reinforced mortar bed occupies the broad waist of this stout ketch. The offset rig keeps ropes clear of the firing arc, while secure magazines and careful anchoring support deliberate bombardment. It opens hostile harbours for the assault craft. Slow handling and a modest direct-fire battery require escorts whenever enemy ships approach.
quote_en: “The wall hears us before it sees us.”

role_en: Deliver raiders to unguarded shores and withdraw before the enemy concentrates.
lore_en: A long, shallow hull combines northern boatbuilding with a practical early modern sail plan. Sweeps carry Draketand through calms, and an open landing deck holds supplies and assault equipment. The vessel raids stores, ferries attackers and retrieves prizes from sheltered beaches. Light construction favours speed and shore access over sustained artillery combat.
quote_en: “A shore is only a door.”

role_en: Supply persistent mass infantry for long campaigns, holding the line with undead clansmen immune to hunger and extreme cold.
lore_en: Frost Clan Levies are dead villagers, retainers and clan warriors who still remember their obligations. Repaired mail, padded wool, old shields and inherited spears give them the appearance of a poor militia. Frost seals their corpse-pale faces and gathers in clothing worn through generations of service. Their strength emerges over a campaign: hunger cannot disperse them, cold cannot drive them indoors, and long marches scarcely interrupt their duty. Each clansman remains a thinking soldier within the persistent mass of the frozen army.
quote_en: “They do not look strong. They simply never stop.”

role_en: Anchor the battle line with disciplined pike ranks that resist cavalry and frontal assault through sustained pressure.
lore_en: Highland Frost Pikes preserve an older way of war through long weapons, layered wool and battered mail or brigandine. Their dead soldiers retain the drill and judgement needed to maintain a wall of points under pressure. Cavalry meets braced shafts; frontal attackers must force their way through ordered ranks. When a soldier is physically destroyed, the next steps forward and closes the gap. Obsolete equipment remains dangerous in the hands of Highlanders whose frozen bodies outlast the exertion of formation warfare.
quote_en: “Kill the first rank. The second is already stepping over them.”

role_en: Press close assaults with heavy blades, remembered technique and undead bodies that endure pain and prolonged combat.
lore_en: Gaelic Frostblades carry clan swordsmanship beyond death. Claymores, broadswords and axes accompany old armour and layered clothing, forming a heavier assault force than the levies. Frozen scars mark faces that remain calm as the fighters advance. Their attacks follow remembered technique and deliberate coordination, sustained by bodies that scarcely respond to fatigue or ordinary pain. Physical destruction can still end their service. Until then, these lucid undead keep pressing a melee with the patience and skill of warriors who remember every lesson.
quote_en: “Their blood slows. Their sword does not.”

class_en: Light Infantry · Bog and Ruin Raiders
role_en: Scout, raid and harass through frozen wetlands, ruins and broken ground with lightly equipped undead infantry.
lore_en: Irish Deadheart Kerns retain a raider’s judgement, moving with short spears, javelins, swords and small shields. Light armour and worn Gaelic clothing distinguish them from the heavier Highland formations. Frozen wetlands, drowned roads and ruined settlements offer routes and positions that living troops cannot occupy for long. The Kerns use that endurance to scout, harass and approach exposed flanks. Their advantage depends on terrain and timing; light equipment leaves them vulnerable when forced into a direct contest with formed heavy infantry.
quote_en: “The marsh froze them. It did not trap them.”

role_en: Support the infantry with primitive matchlock fire, patient watchkeeping and sustained occupation of freezing firing positions.
lore_en: Frost Arquebusiers preserve an early gunpowder tradition through matchlocks, powder flasks and cumbersome old barrels. These weapons remain slow to load and awkward beside modern muskets. Their bearers are intelligent undead who can hold a freezing position through long watches without hunger or the need for warmth. Cold immunity preserves the gunner’s composure, while powder and mechanisms still demand careful handling. Patient volleys provide limited ranged support for an army whose principal strength remains medieval infantry and endurance beyond death.
quote_en: “The powder is old. The patience is older.”

role_en: Hold decisive ground and lead heavy assaults with ancient undead guards, superior armour and absolute battlefield composure.
lore_en: The Hearts of Caledonia are ancient Frost Walkers whose military service has outlasted their own age. Excellent medieval armour, heavy shields, swords and poleaxes distinguish them from every lesser formation. Permanent frost fills the seams of their equipment; dead pale faces retain an almost statue-like awareness. These guards bring remembered duty and disciplined judgement to the army’s hardest positions. They can be physically destroyed, but their protection and composure make that task formidable. Their presence marks the apex of Caledonian endurance.
quote_en: “Their hearts froze. They did not stop.”

role_en: Roam the islands, attack living humans and spread infection, while ignoring the Frost Walkers of Scotland and Ireland.
lore_en: The Wandering Dead roam the British Isles with the remnants of civilian clothing and empty, unrecognising eyes. Thought and identity have vanished, leaving an instinct to attack living humans. Bites and infected wounds spread their condition, turning victims into further mindless undead. They pass Scotland’s and Ireland’s Frost Walkers without attacking them, allowing organised troops to cross infested ground. These hordes obey no military orders. Their presence makes roads, camps and retreats dangerous for living armies, spreading fear and infection beyond any formal battle line.
quote_en: “The dead pass us by. They follow you.”

role_en: Raid flanks, hunt fugitives and descend on isolated guns or baggage with terrifying speed.
lore_en: These riders were once border raiders and clan horsemen before Vestigium cold and undeath remade them into something leaner and crueler. Their horses are half-frozen, half-rotted things that feel neither fatigue nor pity, carrying riders who excel at pursuit, sudden flanking strikes and rear-area terror. They are not meant to win glorious open-field cavalry battles; they exist to appear when retreat begins and turn disorder into massacre.
quote_en: “If you hear the hooves, you are already late.”

role_en: Break morale and foul defended ground by hurling corpses, plague bundles and bound undead masses into enemy positions.
lore_en: The Frost Walkers lack refined artillery doctrine, but they compensate with barbaric ingenuity. Their trebuchets sling frozen cadavers, diseased remains and lash-bound undead packs over walls or into dense formations, combining primitive siegecraft with psychological warfare. The physical damage is sometimes secondary; the true purpose is to poison courage, spread horror and turn every defended position into a place of contamination.
quote_en: “Stone breaks walls. Flesh breaks courage.”

role_en: Track fugitives, screen exposed approaches and pursue scattered living troops with cold-preserved hunting dogs guided by Frost Walker handlers.
lore_en: Frost Hounds preserve the bond between dead huntsmen and the dogs that served them in life. Lean hunting packs follow familiar calls and hand signals, ranging ahead of lightly equipped handlers with spears and worn clan clothing. Frost clings to coarse fur and old leather collars. The packs bring speed and persistence to an army dominated by foot soldiers, harrying isolated enemies and pursuing those who break formation. Their light bodies remain vulnerable to concentrated fire and organised ranks of spears.
quote_en: “He still calls them by their old names.”

role_en: Carry Frost Walkers to hostile anchorages and hold a boarding approach.
lore_en: An old high-sided carrack survives beneath split planks, ice and generations of hurried patches. Frozen crewmen keep its battered rig working long after living sailors would abandon it. Primitive cannon cover a slow approach and the upper castles shelter boarders. Rot still weakens the timbers; the dead can endure a voyage that their hull may not survive.
quote_en: “The crew has already paid the crossing.”

class_en: Undead Coastal Galley · Silent Shore Raids
role_en: Land undead raiders on shallow shores and sustain movement through windless nights.
lore_en: The Grave Galley retains a narrow medieval hull and a damaged lateen rig. Tireless dead rowers move it through sheltered sounds, while a low landing deck delivers kerns close to the waterline. Its few old swivel guns cover withdrawal. Loose seams and a brittle, ice-laden frame restrict rough-water voyages; endless labour cannot restore sound wood.
quote_en: “No dawn relieves the oars.”

role_en: Hold the musket line and steady allied formations through disciplined volleys and veteran bayonet work.
lore_en: Britain’s surviving regulars carry their regimental habits into Castilian service. Patched red coats and maintained flintlocks accompany drill learned before exile, giving allied commanders a dependable line when recruits hesitate. Their small numbers favour carefully chosen positions over broad independent deployments. Castilian supply keeps the companies equipped, while experienced sergeants preserve the cohesion that the loss of their homeland failed to destroy.
quote_en: “We lost the ground. We kept the drill.”

role_en: Secure boarding actions and landing points with experienced British marines fighting alongside Castilian naval forces.
lore_en: The exile marines preserve a profession practised between the gun deck and the shore. Compact muskets, hangers and boarding axes serve in crowded passageways, while disciplined detachments can establish a landing perimeter before heavier troops arrive. Salt-worn coats distinguish them from ceremonial guards. They depend on fleet transport and ammunition from their allies, bringing a scarce reserve of maritime experience to operations where ordinary line infantry struggles.
quote_en: “Give us a rail to cross and a deck to hold.”

role_en: Reconnoitre routes, carry dispatches and screen the movements of exile formations in Castilian service.
lore_en: Britain’s surviving regulars cannot afford a grand cavalry arm, but they still need eyes beyond musket range. The Crown Exile Outriders use hardy horses, practical carbines and disciplined fieldcraft to watch roads, report enemy movement and keep the main body from blundering into danger. Their cavalry is born from necessity rather than prestige, and that makes them more useful than glorious.
quote_en: “We ride so the rest do not march into ruin.”

role_en: Provide the exile contingents with mobile gunfire suited to rapid deployment, hard roads and limited manpower.
lore_en: The British Ruins cannot maintain a lavish artillery arm, so they preserve a small number of light field guns that can follow wherever Castilian service demands. Veteran crews treat each piece as irreplaceable, guarding, repairing and repositioning the guns with grim professionalism. Their battery is modest, but in desperate campaigns, reliability matters more than spectacle.
quote_en: “We cannot waste iron. So we waste nothing.”

role_en: Recover people, archives, relics, weapons and strategic material from areas considered too dangerous for conventional troops.
lore_en: Britain lost cities faster than it could empty them.
