Recovery Sections return to abandoned arsenals, naval offices, universities, estates and government vaults to retrieve whatever the exile command still considers worth risking lives for. Their missions may end with a rescued engineer, a sealed map case or a single crate carried hundreds of miles through territory filled with the dead.
quote_en: “The country is gone. Its memory is not.”

role_en: Enter contaminated ruins and hostile territory ahead of the main force to locate routes, survivors and concentrations of danger.
lore_en: The Pathfinders are veterans who survived long enough in Britain’s dead cities to recognise when a silent street is truly empty and when it merely looks that way. Small teams move ahead of Castilian-aligned columns, marking passages, undead concentrations, unstable structures and defensible fallback positions. Their greatest weapon is accumulated experience from a homeland where a single bad doorway can kill an entire section.
quote_en: “We learned the roads after the roads died.”

class_en: Royal Ship of the Line · Surviving Fleet Relic
role_en: Protect exile convoys and anchor allied squadrons with disciplined broadside fire.
lore_en: One surviving representative of the lost Royal Navy keeps two gun decks, a strong oak hull and a finely balanced sailing rig. Veteran gunners and shipwrights preserve excellent cannon and reliable handling through careful salvage. The ship sails under allied protection, carrying British memory into Castilian service. Every major repair draws on shrinking stores from a kingdom that can no longer replace them.
quote_en: “The kingdom is gone. The watch remains.”

role_en: Form the empire’s main musket line, protecting batteries and advancing through ordered volleys.
lore_en: Crown infantry supplies the regular framework linking distant Portuguese possessions. Wool coats, crossbelts and maintained flintlocks mark companies trained to hold intervals around allied contingents with different weapons. Their officers prize reliable ammunition and recognisable commands over individual display. Imperial endurance treatments help selected soldiers remain effective on long campaigns, but the line still needs food, rest and reinforcement when sustained fire begins to thin its ranks.
quote_en: “Across every ocean, the same command.”

role_en: Seize coastal approaches and hold landing grounds for the empire’s expeditionary forces.
lore_en: Atlantic fusiliers carry compact firearms and boarding blades chosen for boats, piers and shipboard fighting. Their first task ashore is to make room for the next wave, clearing narrow approaches while securing powder and landing stores. They practise alongside naval gun crews and can defend a captured harbour with disciplined musket fire. Long inland pursuits stretch the fleet-based support that makes these soldiers formidable near the coast.
quote_en: “The first boat brings us. The next brings an army.”

role_en: Protect imperial command and hold threatened positions with well-equipped royal heavy infantry.
lore_en: The Lisbon guard preserves an old royal title across an empire whose centres of power now span the Atlantic. Excellent breastplates, swords and selected firearms distinguish its soldiers from ordinary companies. Guard officers commit them where a breach threatens the command group or a contested gateway needs a disciplined counterattack. Their protection is costly and their strength limited, making them a concentrated reserve rather than a substitute for the entire battle line.
quote_en: “A crown travels with those who defend it.”

role_en: Reconnoitre colonial approaches and disrupt enemy movement through dispersed musket fire.
lore_en: Colonial hunters dress for travel rather than parade, combining practical Portuguese firearms with clothing and field knowledge acquired overseas. They read trails, test river crossings and identify concealed positions before the regular infantry advances. Loose spacing limits losses and allows rapid withdrawal through broken ground. Their independence helps expeditions avoid ambush, although scattered hunters need formed troops behind them when an enemy presses a determined assault.
quote_en: “The road begins where the map ends.”

role_en: Screen firearms and batteries from mounted attacks with disciplined spear and pike ranks.
lore_en: Imperial lancers on foot keep a formation weapon useful across an oceanic army of mixed traditions. Long shafts, modest armour and close drill allow them to secure a battery flank or bar an approach while musketeers reload. They offer less flexibility than firearm companies and suffer when artillery fixes them in dense ranks. Their value lies in placing a dependable obstacle exactly where the enemy expects an opening.
quote_en: “Behind these points, the guns reload.”

role_en: Lead difficult breaches with experienced assault infantry strengthened by controlled Vestigium treatment.
lore_en: The reborn conquistadores are veterans returned to demanding service through Vestigium-enhanced endurance. Worn cuirasses, heavy blades and short firearms support deliberate assaults into defended entrances and narrow streets. Their improvement lengthens useful service without removing wounds or exhaustion from the campaign. Officers value the judgement these soldiers accumulated before treatment, committing them to objectives whose capture requires close coordination more than a reckless rush.
quote_en: “Another campaign. The same scar.”

role_en: Hold critical ground through prolonged fighting with the empire’s most enduring heavy guards.
lore_en: The longevity guard represents the patient side of imperial Vestigium practice. Excellent armour protects soldiers whose treatments extend stamina and useful years, allowing a veteran core to survive repeated campaigning. They stand around magazines, command posts and narrow passages where steady resistance matters. Maintaining their equipment and treatment is expensive. Their bodies remain mortal, and commanders must distinguish exceptional endurance from an unlimited capacity to absorb injury.
quote_en: “Time has more work for us.”

role_en: Support imperial assaults with allied Mexica close infantry and coordinated shield attacks.
lore_en: Mexica warriors retain quilted protection, distinctive shields and broad striking weapons within the Portuguese alliance. Their companies close after supporting fire disrupts the enemy, using local coordination to force short, violent contests around obstacles. Imperial contact brings metal fittings and selected replacement weapons without erasing their martial identity. They remain dependent on reaching close range, making exposed advances against settled musket fire their hardest assignment.
quote_en: “Open the way. We will take the last steps.”

role_en: Strike exposed enemy flanks with selected Mexica eagle warriors trained for rapid close assault.
lore_en: Eagle guards combine elite Mexica identity with equipment adapted through imperial alliance. Restrained feather insignia identifies selected fighters whose shields and edged weapons favour a swift attack against a shaken position. They work beside scouts and supporting firearms, choosing a vulnerable angle before closing. Their status rests on disciplined aggression and experience, while conspicuous insignia and light protection make prolonged exposure to enemy volleys especially dangerous.
quote_en: “Watch the flank after the thunder.”

role_en: Break resistance in confined ground with protected Mexica jaguar assault guards.
lore_en: Jaguar guards carry heavy close weapons behind strong shields and quilted armour marked by restrained feline patterns. They are assigned to entrances, barricades and short approaches where their cohesion can survive the final rush. Unlike the more mobile eagle companies, they concentrate on sustained contact after the first impact. Their imposing identity lends weight to an assault, but neither patterned armour nor reputation can replace covering fire across open ground.
quote_en: “The gate is narrow enough.”

role_en: Guide and support imperial infantry through dense vegetation and broken colonial terrain.
lore_en: Maya allied warriors bring knowledge of paths, concealed approaches and local supplies to formations that European drill alone cannot sustain. Layered cotton clothing, modest shields and practical blades favour movement through close terrain. Their groups identify ambush sites and fight around obstacles while regular troops secure the wider line. They lose much of this advantage when forced onto exposed ground against concentrated artillery and ordered musket companies.
quote_en: “The forest has its own roads.”

role_en: Disrupt exposed troops with concealed bow fire from carefully chosen local approaches.
lore_en: Maya archers operate with small shields, light cotton protection and bows suited to dispersed shooting. Their arrows preserve a missile option when powder is scarce or firing reveals a position too early. They watch crossings and narrow approaches, withdrawing before heavy troops force contact. Imperial commanders use them to disturb movement and prepare an assault rather than expecting arrows alone to defeat disciplined armoured formations.
quote_en: “The first warning is already behind you.”

role_en: Locate hostile movements and safe routes through independent Apache frontier reconnaissance.
lore_en: Apache scouts serve the imperial coalition through observation, tracking and patient movement rather than parade-ground conformity. Practical clothing, bows or selected firearms and compact equipment allow them to work ahead of larger columns. Their reports reveal trails, concealed camps and opportunities for withdrawal. Officers must give scouts room to use local judgement; forcing them into a regular musket line wastes the very expertise for which they were recruited.
quote_en: “We have already seen the camp.”

role_en: Carry out distant imperial landings with elite infantry supplied by the Black Ships.
lore_en: Black-Ship expeditionaries are selected for campaigns beyond familiar ports, where a lost landing store can matter as much as a lost engagement. Durable dark coats, firearms, blades and compact field kits suit shipboard travel followed by immediate action ashore. Their training joins independent judgement to disciplined small detachments. Endurance treatments support demanding expeditions, while ammunition and transport still bind their striking power to the ships that brought them.
quote_en: “The ship leaves when the work is done.”

role_en: Lead boarding detachments and preserve control during the Black Ships’ hardest close engagements.
lore_en: Black-Ship captains fight close enough for orders to survive the noise of boarding. Fine but practical armour, pistols and strong swords accompany officers chosen for seamanship and assault judgement. Their guard forms around access points, rallying scattered expeditionaries before a captured deck becomes a secure position. Authority depends on keeping the vessel, crew and mission together. Losing these leaders can unravel an operation far from imperial reinforcement.
quote_en: “Hold the ladder. I will hold the men.”

role_en: Exploit broken formations and protect imperial columns with mobile colonial cavalry.
lore_en: Overseas cavalry keeps equipment light enough for extended patrols: carbines, sabres, leather harness and coats worn hard by travel. Riders watch the flanks of marching columns and gather prisoners after infantry or artillery opens a gap. Their effectiveness rests on healthy remounts and access to forage across colonial routes. They can turn a retreat into a rout, but a prepared line of bayonets remains a costly target.
quote_en: “A broken line still has miles left to run.”

role_en: Harass exposed supply routes and pursue vulnerable detachments with fast Apache mounted raiders.
lore_en: Apache horsemen use speed and flexible grouping to reach isolated wagons, couriers and scattered troops. Bows, carbines and short blades give them several ways to strike without remaining under settled fire. Their riding equipment is practical, with small loads and few ceremonial fittings. They are valuable for extending imperial reconnaissance and pursuit, while healthy horses and space to disengage remain essential to their way of war.
quote_en: “A wagon cannot watch every horizon.”

role_en: Engage enemy batteries and distant formations with long-barrel imperial cannon.
lore_en: Imperial culverin crews work around slender bronze or iron barrels whose reach shapes the opening artillery exchange. Gunners prepare stable positions, measure charges and conserve valuable ammunition for targets that justify the shot. Their long pieces require substantial transport and protection while changing position. The advantage is deliberate reach: commanders can pressure hostile batteries before sending infantry into the ground those guns were meant to dominate.
quote_en: “Let their guns answer from farther away.”

role_en: Reduce fortified positions with enormous crown siege cannon and carefully prepared firing works.
lore_en: Basilisk batteries embody the empire’s willingness to move extraordinary weight for a decisive siege. Massive barrels, reinforced carriages and specialised crews demand roads, draft animals and large powder stocks before a shot can be fired. Their crews build firing beds and protect the mechanism from uneven recoil. Once established, the battery threatens masonry and fixed defences, but its cumbersome movement makes a collapsing field position disastrous.
quote_en: “The road was built for this shot.”

role_en: Provide heavy ship-derived gunfire against coastal works and defended landing approaches.
lore_en: Naval bombard crews bring the habits of the gun deck into imperial shore operations. Thick naval barrels, heavy tackle and practiced loading teams allow them to support an attack once a stable platform is secured. Sailors manage recoil, powder handling and damaged fittings with tools carried from their ships. Their strength is concentrated fire near maritime supply; inland deployment quickly turns gun weight and ammunition into a severe transport problem.
quote_en: “The gun deck has come ashore.”

role_en: Investigate cult activity, Vestigium contamination and supernatural outbreaks before they compromise colonial administration.
lore_en: The Overseas Inquisitors are feared less for religious ceremony than for the authority they carry. A small team may quarantine a settlement, interrogate an expedition, destroy a corrupted artefact or order an infected outpost abandoned before an outbreak spreads along imperial shipping routes. They exist because an oceanic empire cannot afford to let one hidden anomaly travel aboard the wrong vessel.
quote_en: “An empire of oceans cannot permit one infected ship.”

role_en: Operate for months beyond reliable imperial supply to map, scout, raid, rescue and open routes through unknown territory.
lore_en: The old bandeirante tradition survives in a colder and far larger Portuguese Empire. These modern frontier bands penetrate regions where roads vanish, maps contradict one another and established garrisons cannot follow. Their members are explorers, hunters and soldiers in equal measure, capable of crossing entire provinces with little more support than what they can carry, trade for or take from the land.
quote_en: “The map ends before we do.”

role_en: Locate, secure and extract dangerous Vestigium objects before rivals, cults or uncontrolled settlements can exploit them.
lore_en: Portuguese expansion reaches too many forgotten ruins and isolated territories for conventional armies to investigate every discovery. Relic Hunters operate as compact expeditionary teams combining scholarship, fieldcraft and armed containment. Their task is rarely to understand a Vestigium completely; it is to ensure that the Crown possesses it before somebody more reckless does.
quote_en: “Find it first. Understand it later.”

role_en: Lead imperial battle squadrons through sustained heavy exchanges.
lore_en: A broad black hull carries three gun decks beneath dark canvas. Reinforced framing and deep stores support long ocean crossings before the first shot is fired. Captains seek deliberate broadside contests backed by escorts; heavy draught and immense maintenance needs keep the ship dependent on imperial arsenals.
quote_en: “The horizon wears our colours.”

name_native: NAU DE LINHA LEÃO DO MAR
role_en: Hold the battle line and cover the empire’s most valuable convoys.
lore_en: Leão do Mar concentrates two useful batteries in a strong, ocean-ready hull. Lower galleries and a balanced rig improve handling beside heavier flagships. It can escort colonial traffic without surrendering its place in a fleet action. Long deployments wear its dark canvas and require reliable repair stations along the route.
quote_en: “Our cargo sails behind our guns.”

role_en: Escort dispersed ocean traffic and drive off approaching raiders.
lore_en: A long black hull carries one covered battery, strong boats and generous freshwater stowage. Sombra Atlântica remains with merchant groups after heavier escorts turn home. Its guns deter light attackers and its rig keeps contact across changing winds. Confronting a battle squadron would sacrifice the mobility on which its protection depends.
quote_en: “The shadow keeps pace.”

role_en: Capture isolated merchantmen and withdraw with profitable prizes.
lore_en: Dente de Noite combines a compact brig rig with a clear deck for prize parties. Chase guns cut a merchant’s escape while grappling gear prepares the final approach. Captains choose valuable, weakly escorted targets. Crowded prize crews and limited stores force frequent returns to friendly colonial ports.
quote_en: “The richest flag is the slowest.”

role_en: Inspect colonial approaches and warn settlements of hostile sails.
lore_en: An adaptable lateen rig and moderate draught suit the broken shorelines of imperial colonies. Guarda-Costas watches anchorages, carries patrol boats and boards suspect traders under light gun cover. Its crews know local bars and currents. Small magazines and light planking make warning the fleet wiser than challenging a heavy intruder.
quote_en: “Every inlet has a witness.”

role_en: Screen transports and repel small craft around a convoy.
lore_en: Vigia Negra keeps a compact square rig above a nimble black hull. A modest battery and quick-loading swivel pieces cover the convoy’s nearest approaches. The ship repeatedly changes station to answer threats that a heavy escort cannot chase. Restricted endurance and a small crew demand careful watch rotations on extended voyages.
quote_en: “The convoy has no blind side.”

role_en: Move soldiers, mounts and campaign stores between imperial ports.
lore_en: Broad hatches, temporary troop decks and lifting tackle give Travessia its purpose. Black sails and a few defensive guns keep it recognisably imperial without consuming its cargo space. It delivers a force ready to unload together. Crowded passages and heavy loading make sickness, weather and delayed escort schedules strategic threats.
quote_en: “An empire arrives in the hold.”

role_en: Survey distant routes and sustain imperial missions beyond settled ports.
lore_en: Estrela Austral favours stores, spare spars and survey boats over a dense battery. Its dark hull is built for long crossings and repair by its own carpenters. Navigators chart shelter before the next expedition follows. Months away from an arsenal magnify ordinary damage; knowledge of the route becomes the vessel’s strongest protection.
quote_en: “Find the harbour before the army needs it.”

role_en: Suppress hostile coastal works with deliberate mortar fire.
lore_en: A strong central bed carries a heavy mortar clear of the ketch’s rigging. Cinza Real anchors under escort and works against batteries that block imperial landings. Protected powder compartments and restrained sail area reduce risk during firing. Its slow movement and weak broadside expose it whenever the enemy navy can close.
quote_en: “Stone makes a poor roof.”

role_en: Bring attackers through shoals and alongside coastal targets.
lore_en: A low black-painted hull carries sweeps, a small dark sail and a strengthened bow platform. Ponta Negra works from transports, crossing the water their draught denies them. Grapnels and light guns cover the last few yards. Its men and equipment fill the open hull quickly, leaving little margin for a rough sea or sustained gunfire.
quote_en: “The last yard belongs to the oars.”

role_en: Deliver controlled musket fire and defend Company positions with salaried British regulars.
lore_en: Company redcoats draw strength from maintained flintlocks, paid drill and stores purchased before the campaign begins. Their long coats and regimented cartridge equipment suit a professional line that protects depots and supports expansion from fortified settlements. Commercial priorities determine where they serve, but officers expect military discipline once fire opens. They are dependable in formed combat and costly to replace when a distant expedition outruns its supply.
quote_en: “The accounts are settled after the line holds.”

role_en: Guard warehouses, treasuries and convoy stores against raids and local unrest.
lore_en: Merchant-house guards are organised around the assets that keep Company warfare solvent. Compact muskets, sturdy coats and practical watch equipment suit gates, yards and wagon parks more than open-field manoeuvre. Experienced guards know who belongs inside a storehouse and how to bar its approaches. They release regular regiments for campaigning, though static duty and limited field practice make them a weaker choice for aggressive infantry assaults.
quote_en: “Nothing leaves this gate uncounted.”

role_en: Break defended entrances and reinforce close assaults with selected Company grenadiers.
lore_en: Company grenadiers receive sturdy firearms, grenades and robust equipment for the final approach to a defended position. Their detachments rehearse working around walls and narrow entrances, with supporting volleys covering the advance. Selection favours composure and strength rather than height alone. They provide concentrated assault power to a wealthy army, but explosives and veteran recruits are expensive resources to spend on an objective that ordinary manoeuvre could secure.
quote_en: “One doorway. One clear order.”

role_en: Maintain the Company’s broad infantry line through trained Indian musket regiments.
lore_en: Sepoy regiments combine Indian recruitment and local command relationships with professional firearm drill. Practical turbans, tailored tunics and standard cartridge equipment accompany muskets maintained through Company arsenals. Their strength lets the army hold more than a handful of European garrisons, while familiarity with language and local conditions supports campaigning. Cohesion depends on reliable pay, respected officers and consistent orders across formations with different customs.
quote_en: “The musket drill belongs to every man in the rank.”

role_en: Keep Indian regiments coherent through veteran leadership and local tactical judgement.
lore_en: Subedar veterans bring experienced Indian officers and senior soldiers to the centre of Company field command. Fine practical tunics, swords and selected firearms distinguish men expected to translate orders into action when younger troops falter. They understand the regiments’ habits and keep detachments working through broken terrain or disrupted communications. Their value is difficult to replace: a lost leader removes both military experience and a trusted link within the ranks.
quote_en: “They know my voice before the drum.”

role_en: Provide a protected Indian elite reserve through allied royal household guards.
lore_en: The Maharaja’s guard retains courtly armour, fine blades and household discipline within the Company’s coalition. These troops serve under negotiated obligations, giving commanders a strong close-combat reserve without dissolving their royal identity into redcoat drill. Their guards can protect a command group or contest a narrow breach. Excellent equipment and loyalty make them formidable, while limited numbers and allied authority shape where the Company may employ them.
quote_en: “Our oath arrived before the contract.”

role_en: Raid hostile shipping, seize cargo and conduct deniable coastal operations under Company letters of marque.
lore_en: Company Freebooters are sailors, smugglers, deserters and professional raiders from ports across four continents who accepted Company charters in exchange for pay, safe harbour and a lawful share of captured wealth. They board merchantmen, intercept couriers, sabotage quays and perform operations regular troops cannot acknowledge. Crews preserve their own languages and weapons while Company agents standardise signals, prize rules and objectives. Their loyalty is commercial rather than patriotic, but a contract honoured for years can bind harder than a flag.
quote_en: “The Crown gave us laws. The Company gave us a share.”

class_en: Asian Freebooters · Night Boarding & Strait Warfare
role_en: Control narrow seas through night boarding, concealed approaches and fast strikes against anchored shipping.
lore_en: The Malacca Black Flags draw Malay, Bugis, Chinese, Indian and other Asian sailors into compact crews built for the straits. Dark sailcloth, muffled fittings and shallow-draft craft let them approach at night before pistols, blades and boarding hooks settle the fight at arm’s length. They know currents, mangrove channels and harbour habits better than most regular officers. Their weakness is open-water battle against heavier warships, where stealth and local knowledge matter less than broadside weight.
quote_en: “In the strait, darkness has the right of way.”

role_en: Capture valuable ships intact through aggressive boarding, grenade work and disciplined deck fighting.
lore_en: Atlantic Corsairs are drawn largely from British, Irish, French, Dutch, Iberian and colonial seafaring communities that found Company service more profitable than allegiance to a single crown. Flintlocks, cutlasses, boarding axes and grenades support a direct style of ship seizure in which the prize is worth more afloat than sunk. Veteran crews train to overwhelm gun decks and rigging access before defenders can organise. Their confidence becomes costly when a target carries more soldiers than cargo.
quote_en: “Do not sink what the Company can sell.”

role_en: Raid shallow coasts and river approaches beyond the safe reach of deep-draft Company warships.
lore_en: Guinea Coast Reavers recruit African sailors, coastal fighters and river pilots whose experience lets Company raiding parties move where ocean-going vessels cannot. Longboats and captured local craft carry muskets, spears and heavy boarding blades into estuaries, creeks and trading settlements. Endurance and route knowledge make them excellent at cutting warehouses and communications away from fortified harbours. They are raiders rather than line infantry, and prolonged occupation wastes the mobility that makes them valuable.
quote_en: “The large ship stops where our work begins.”

role_en: Ambush convoys, seize officers and destroy supplies through fast boat actions and accurate irregular fire.
lore_en: The Red Jacks recruit from Caribbean ports and American colonial routes where sailors, hunters and smugglers already understand how to disappear between islands. Accurate muskets, pistols and light boats support ambushes against dispatch vessels, convoy escorts and exposed shore stores. They prefer prisoners, maps and powder to glorious deck duels, because intelligence and interrupted supply often earn the Company more than a burned hull. Heavy fleet actions leave their scattered crews dangerously outgunned.
quote_en: “Take the captain alive. Burn only what cannot be carried.”

role_en: Secure trading ports and shipboard access with professional Company marine detachments.
lore_en: Company marines stand where commerce meets armed resistance: quays, merchant decks, harbour gates and contested landing points. Compact flintlocks, boarding weapons and weatherproof powder storage favour action around vessels and warehouses. They escort valuable cargo and establish safe access for reinforcements. Their skills make trade routes defensible, although long inland campaigning removes the maritime support and confined-ground advantages around which their training is built.
quote_en: “A safe harbour is defended from both sides.”

role_en: Break weakened infantry, contest hostile cavalry and give the Company a true heavy mounted option.
lore_en: Where Company money meets local martial tradition, heavy cavalry survives in altered form. Zirah Sawaran ride under scale, mail or plated protection with lances, sabres and pistols, providing a more armoured answer than the lighter mounted arms of the Company. They are not numerous, but they lend prestige, battlefield weight and a respectable shock arm to an army otherwise built around commerce, contracts and gunpowder.
quote_en: “Some contracts are signed in iron.”

role_en: Screen wide frontiers, harass exposed lines and respond quickly where the Company cannot wait for formal cavalry concentration.
lore_en: Not every mounted problem in India can be answered by parade-ground drill. Silladar horsemen bring lighter equipment, faster local reaction and more individual initiative to the Company’s campaigns, making them valuable in broken country, fast raids and confused marches. They are less tidy than European cavalry, but in the places where imperial control is weakest, they are often the first mounted force that matters.
quote_en: “By the time the clerk records us, we are already elsewhere.”

role_en: Provide the Company with broad-spectrum Indian cavalry for scouting, escort, pursuit and general battlefield service.
lore_en: Sowar regiments form the dependable middle of the Company’s mounted arm. Recruited locally and trained to work alongside infantry and guns, they are adaptable rather than glamorous, able to screen a column in the morning and join a pursuit by afternoon. Their strength lies in practical service, local experience and the ability to do many cavalry jobs well enough for imperial campaigning.
quote_en: “Useful first, glorious later.”

role_en: Deliver disciplined mobile firepower, reinforce threatened sectors and pursue with professional mounted carbines.
lore_en: The Company’s best European-style cavalry arm is built around money, drill and superior equipment. Chartered Dragoons ride good horses, carry quality carbines and pistols, and are trained to fight mounted or dismounted as contract and terrain require. Expensive, efficient and unmistakably corporate, they embody the Company’s habit of solving military problems by buying professionalism at scale.
quote_en: “The Company pays for speed, and for accuracy.”

role_en: Support Company infantry with accurately served field cannon and dependable ammunition supply.
lore_en: Company artillery turns financial depth into maintained barrels, organised limbers and trained gun crews. Gunners prepare measured charges and coordinate fire with infantry movements instead of treating each cannon as an isolated possession. Their batteries can shift pressure across the line when roads and draft teams permit. Precision relies on survey, ammunition and repair stores; losing that support turns expensive equipment into a stationary burden.
quote_en: “The range is measured. The bill can wait.”

class_en: Company Exceptional Corps · One Hundred Numbered Seats
role_en: Deploy standardised Vestigium specialists against threats beyond the capability of ordinary Company formations.
lore_en: After sustained trade with Castilia, Company observers attempted to reproduce the strategic utility of the numbered Royal Guard without depending on irreplaceable individuals. The Chartered Hundred consists of one hundred numbered offices built around documented Vestigium systems, specialised weapons and strict bearer requirements. A Castilian Number belongs to a person; a Company Seat belongs to the institution. When a bearer dies, the Charter, equipment and accumulated doctrine pass to a successor. Individual Seats rarely match the supernatural ceiling of the true Royal Guard, but the Company considers continuity the more useful miracle.
quote_en: “The bearer may die. The Charter remains.”

role_en: Coordinate the Company’s most dangerous privateer flotillas through captains trusted with exceptional independence.
lore_en: The Black Charter is not a regiment but a compact between the Company and a select circle of privateer captains whose reputations span oceans. Each captain commands a vessel or small flotilla under unusually broad authority, choosing routes and methods so long as Company objectives and prize obligations are met. They can combine Asian pilots, Atlantic boarders, African river crews and Caribbean raiders into temporary strike groups without forcing them into one culture. Their independence makes them extraordinarily adaptive and politically dangerous if trust ever breaks.
quote_en: “The Company owns the contract. The sea still belongs to us.”

class_en: Armoured Steam-Sail Capital Ship · Convoy Deterrence
role_en: Keep major convoys open against organised enemy squadrons.
lore_en: A plated central battery and heavy broadside guns give the Company an armoured capital presence. Sailing masts conserve fuel between contracted depots. Protection is concentrated around machinery and magazines, leaving the ends vulnerable. It cannot match Castilia’s second-generation turret ships in a moving duel; its value lies in guarding traffic where their scarce hulls cannot be everywhere.
quote_en: “The dividend travels behind armour.”

role_en: Protect remote trade routes and concentrate quickly against raiders.
lore_en: Iron Ledger carries selective plating over a long cruiser hull. Auxiliary steam breaks a calm or secures contact, while sail pays for the long patrol. A mixed medium battery suits commerce protection rather than fleet duels. Boiler specialists and replacement plates must follow the same routes as the merchants it guards.
quote_en: “Every mile has an owner.”

role_en: Shift between threatened convoys without waiting for a favourable breeze.
lore_en: A compact engine installation helps Sentinel hold station around valuable merchantmen. Strong bows and a useful single-deck battery withstand ordinary raiders. Light machinery protection keeps displacement manageable, but sustained heavy fire can end its advantage. Captains reserve coal for the hours when wind alone would miss the contract.
quote_en: “On time is a fighting quality.”

role_en: Provide durable battle-line support from the Company’s Indian yards.
lore_en: Indian master builders shape tough teak into a carefully fastened two-decker. A balanced rig and consistent battery reward professional gunnery instead of unusual machinery. Its long service life makes purchase costly and maintenance economical. The ship remains dependent on wind and cannot force contact with an advanced steam opponent.
quote_en: “A sound keel outlives a contract.”

role_en: Guard Indian Ocean convoys through long monsoon passages.
lore_en: Garuda joins fine Indian timber work to an escort frigate’s long waterline. Strong deck framing supports a covered battery and ample boat stowage. Experienced local navigators read seasonal crossings and regional harbours. Its excellent endurance does not supply battleship protection; avoiding a heavy squadron remains part of the escort plan.
quote_en: “The season changes. The keel holds.”

role_en: Carry high-value cargo while resisting opportunistic attacks.
lore_en: Broad holds, a high stern and defensive gun decks make this merchantman expensive prey. Its stout hull protects the cargo that finances Company war. Cannon placements support convoy defence, while commercial loading shapes every voyage. Extra guns reduce paying capacity; crowded holds and a wide turning circle limit aggressive pursuit.
quote_en: “The profit can answer back.”

role_en: Carry ordinary cargo and reinforce the convoy’s defensive perimeter.
lore_en: A lighter merchant hull carries enough cannon to make several Indiamen mutually supporting. Crews drill together before seasonal departures, keeping simple signals and common convoy speeds. This distributed defence frustrates isolated raiders. Sailing qualities vary with cargo, so the slowest loaded ship often fixes the whole convoy’s pace.
quote_en: “No merchant sails alone.”

role_en: Move bulk naval stores between depots at low operating cost.
lore_en: A purchased Dutch-derived fluyt offers a capacious hold beneath a narrow working deck. Company fittings add light defensive cannon and secure powder stowage. Economical handling releases trained sailors for combat ships. Its weak battery and cargo-first hull demand escort wherever a privateer can intercept the route.
quote_en: “War also travels by the barrel.”

role_en: Reinforce battle screens with a well-maintained purchased prize.
lore_en: A Dutch-built frigate enters Company service with its original hull lines intact. Standardised shot stores and new signals make the captured ship useful beside British and Indian-built escorts. Spare fittings remain awkward to procure. Its experienced mixed crew supplies skill, but differences in construction complicate repairs far from the refit yard.
quote_en: “A new charter. The same good ship.”

role_en: Seize enemy commerce under a Company-backed commission.
lore_en: This quick brig mounts chase pieces and carries prize gear instead of heavy protection. Its contract rewards capture, encouraging careful target choice and rapid disengagement. Company ports receive prisoners and redistribute taken cargo. Prize crews drain its manpower, and disputes over ownership can keep a successful ship idle at anchor.
quote_en: “Sign here. Lose the cargo there.”

role_en: Harass exposed depots and intercept light merchant traffic.
lore_en: A former pirate hull keeps the shallow draught and quick rig that made it hard to catch. A corporate refit improves magazines and discipline without erasing its irregular habits. Captains exploit channels larger escorts avoid. Thin planking and small provisions restrict prolonged gunfights and operations far from a friendly inlet.
quote_en: “The coast keeps no receipts.”

role_en: Attack through narrow coastal approaches with concentrated forward fire.
lore_en: A pointed grab bow carries useful chase guns ahead of a compact Indian-built hull. Sail and sweeps manoeuvre it through coastal calms. Local crews exploit currents before closing on a vulnerable target. Its forward emphasis sacrifices broadside weight, making a prolonged beam-to-beam contest against a frigate a poor bargain.
quote_en: “The bow makes the first argument.”

class_en: Steam River Gunboat · Inland Fire Support
role_en: Escort river convoys and suppress defended banks.
lore_en: A shallow hull supports a compact protected boiler and a heavy forward gun. Paddle propulsion gives control against current where sailing escorts struggle. River crews survey bars before loaded transports follow. Exposed wheels and limited coal storage constrain combat; a damaged channel chart can matter as much as an enemy gun.
quote_en: “The river is a supply road.”

role_en: Guard depot entrances and respond to armed intrusions.
lore_en: Harbour Warrant concentrates protective plates around a light gun and its machinery. A compact steam drive frees it from the harbour breeze. Depot crews maintain it near fuel and workshops, making short patrols dependable. Low freeboard and cramped bunkers keep it tied to protected water rather than an ocean station.
quote_en: “The gate carries a gun.”

role_en: Reduce coastal batteries that obstruct a chartered landing.
lore_en: A reinforced mortar bed and secure magazines give this hired bomb ketch a narrow but valuable purpose. Company surveyors choose anchorages and prepare ammunition before the firing day. Its owners charge for the damage a bombardment imposes on hull and rig. Slow handling leaves it dependent on escorts throughout the siege.
quote_en: “The invoice arrives after the shell.”

role_en: Deliver contracted regiments and their stores as one organised force.
lore_en: A hybrid transport uses sail for the voyage and steam to hold the final approach schedule. Wide hatches, removable troop decks and lifting tackle carry soldiers with their campaign equipment. Its defensive guns protect embarkation rather than win a battle. Crowding, coal and freshwater compete for the same valuable carrying space.
quote_en: “The regiment lands with its tools.”

role_en: Supply coal and engine stores to dispersed modern squadrons.
lore_en: This heavy storeship carries divided fuel holds, spare machinery and strong transfer boats. Sail keeps its own coal expenditure modest. Contracted rendezvous let steam escorts remain on station without returning to an arsenal. A slow, dirty cargo operation needs sheltered water; missing the collier can silence an otherwise powerful cruiser.
quote_en: “An empty bunker voids the threat.”

role_en: Map channels and identify anchorages before the fleet commits.
lore_en: Sea Surveyor carries sounding boats, lead lines and spare markers beneath a manageable brig rig. Its officers translate local pilots’ knowledge into charts Company captains can share. Light cannon protect a working party. Surveying requires slow, exposed movement near unfamiliar banks, so discoveries cost time that admirals must allow.
quote_en: “Measure the water before spending the fleet.”

role_en: Move orders and intelligence between separated Company stations.
lore_en: A generous fore-and-aft rig drives a narrow, shallow hull. Express Bond carries secure dispatch lockers and light signalling gear instead of cargo or a fighting battery. Couriers keep convoy contracts aligned across distant ports. Its speed depends on weather, and the tiny crew has little margin for damage or a long pursuit.
quote_en: “News earns its passage.”

role_en: Intercept isolated shipping along routes known to its contracted crew.
lore_en: A battered Dutch-derived raider returned from an abandoned route with a veteran crew and a reputation for appearing out of sea mist. Company refits preserve its low profile and quiet handling. Concealed boarding gear supports capture. The Flying Dutchman stories sell fear; worn frames, ordinary guns and demanding repairs still set its limits.
quote_en: “Some debts return with the tide.”

role_en: Advance through aggressive musket volleys to fix the enemy for An Nam’s concentrated guns and assault reserves.
lore_en: Imperial musket infantry carries older firearms in tightly coordinated formations. Indigo tunics, repaired stocks and economical cartridge equipment reflect an army investing heavily in numbers and artillery. Their drill favours closing the decision quickly, with successive volleys supporting a purposeful advance. Courage cannot shorten loading time, so officers coordinate movement with the batteries and spear companies that keep an aggressive infantry line from becoming an exposed target.
quote_en: “Old guns. A very short distance.”

role_en: Open the attack and seize weak points before the opposing line can reorganise.
lore_en: Vanguard troops travel with lighter loads than the main line, carrying short blades and selected firearms for a fast final approach. They follow reconnaissance and artillery preparation, aiming at a gateway, flank or wavering company rather than an entire front. Their aggression buys time for supporting formations to arrive. A failed first attack leaves lightly supplied detachments exposed, making clear objectives and prompt reinforcement essential.
quote_en: “Take the opening while it is still open.”

role_en: Protect imperial command and provide a disciplined elite infantry reserve for decisive engagements.
lore_en: The imperial guard combines fine lacquered protection with practical blades and maintained firearms. Selection favours soldiers able to keep formation as orders change, allowing the court’s household troops to serve as a battlefield instrument as well as a symbol of authority. They counterattack threatened positions and stabilise a rapid offensive. Their limited strength demands careful commitment after scouts and regular infantry reveal where the decision can be forced.
quote_en: “The order reaches us once.”

role_en: Force close combat against defended infantry with armoured dao-bearing assault troops.
lore_en: Armoured blade infantry carries broad dao swords behind iron lamellar and padded cloth. The equipment protects the final approach and gives weight to sustained fighting around gates, obstacles and broken ranks. Their companies advance with supporting fire rather than racing the musketeers. Heavy kit slows movement and consumes strength, so commanders reserve these fighters for a short, deliberate collision after artillery has already damaged the position.
quote_en: “The guns open it. The blades enter.”

role_en: Protect musket companies and artillery from mounted pressure with long spear formations.
lore_en: Long-spear companies provide a dependable barrier within An Nam’s rapid offensives. Modest helmets and layered indigo clothing leave resources for durable shafts, close drill and replacement weapons. They secure flanks while firearms reload and occupy passages that an enemy might use to counterattack. Their strength depends on cohesion; distant gunfire and broken footing can dismantle a wall of points before it reaches a useful position.
quote_en: “Keep the points level. Keep the road closed.”

role_en: Close with disrupted positions and break them using hỏa hổ projectors, sulphur bombs and short-range assault weapons.
lore_en: Hỏa Hổ assault troops carry incendiary projectors, sulphur fire-bombs, short firearms and heavy blades into the final approach. They follow artillery or elephant shock into breaches where smoke, flame and panic can collapse defenders faster than musket drill alone. Veteran crews learn to handle volatile mixtures while moving through gates, trenches and dense streets. Their killing power is brutal at close range, but exposed fuel and limited reach make a failed approach exceptionally costly.
quote_en: “Close enough to see the fire. Too close to stop it.”

role_en: Keep the artillery offensive moving through repairs, route preparation and powder handling.
lore_en: Artillery engineers carry wheel fittings, tools and measuring rods alongside modest personal weapons. They reinforce crossings, repair carriages and organise the stores that sustain An Nam’s concentrated fire. Their work often determines whether an ambitious advance reaches its next objective with guns or merely with tired infantry. The corps remains vulnerable while working, requiring guards when a road repair or damaged limber brings the column to a halt.
quote_en: “A broken wheel can stop a victory.”

role_en: Locate approaches and hostile positions before An Nam commits its fast-moving formations.
lore_en: Mountain scouts wear muted cloth and carry light firearms, blades and compact travel stores. They work ahead of the army, reading paths and identifying places where a large formation or elephant corps would become trapped. Their reports guide the rapid concentration of troops and guns. Small groups move flexibly through difficult ground, but limited ammunition and protection favour observation and withdrawal over prolonged fighting with formed infantry.
quote_en: “Fast armies still need a safe path.”

role_en: Support close assaults through dense terrain with Khmer allied infantry.
lore_en: Khmer auxiliary guards retain woven regional dress and familiar short blades within An Nam’s combined army. Their groups work through narrow paths, clearing obstacles and approaching positions that a broad musket line cannot easily reach. Allied officers maintain local cohesion while coordinating with imperial fire support. Their equipment suits close ground, with less protection and reach when ordered into a frontal contest on an exposed field.
quote_en: “There is room for a blade along this path.”

role_en: Secure hill approaches and guide spear formations through broken upland ground.
lore_en: Lao highland spears use compact shields and long weapons with woven layers suited to demanding travel. They guard elevated paths and contest approaches where dense cavalry or heavy guns struggle to manoeuvre. Their value includes guiding allied columns and warning of movement through secondary routes. Commanders gain reliable local infantry by respecting their formation habits, while extended operations far from familiar supply reduce their effectiveness.
quote_en: “The slope decides how many can come.”

role_en: Provide disciplined Siamese allied infantry for coordinated assaults and secure defensive positions.
lore_en: Siamese royal auxiliaries bring maintained firearms, blades and selected armour to the imperial coalition. Household training gives their companies a steadier formation than improvised levies, allowing them to hold a captured point while the offensive moves onward. Their regional insignia and command relationships remain visible within common campaign orders. An Nam gains experienced allies, but their deployment must account for royal obligations and the support required to maintain their equipment.
quote_en: “Our colours remain. Our orders agree.”

role_en: Press short close attacks with Burmese allied infantry after supporting fire disrupts resistance.
lore_en: Burmese vanguard companies carry dha blades, shields and selected old firearms in compact assault groups. Their practical clothing and reduced baggage favour a determined approach through broken ground. They exploit confusion created by the empire’s guns, forcing defenders to choose between keeping formation and answering nearby blades. Sustained musket exchanges waste their strengths, so officers give these troops a clear approach, a close objective and prompt support.
quote_en: “The last few steps belong to us.”

role_en: Exploit the decisive opening with An Nam’s fastest and most disciplined guard reserve.
lore_en: The rapid guard is selected for coordinated movement under changing orders. Lightened protection, fine blades and compact firearms allow its soldiers to reach a threatened or newly opened point before slower formations. They finish a breakthrough or recover a position whose loss would halt the offensive. Their distinction is timing and judgement, supported by scouts and clear communication. Repeated commitment exhausts a scarce reserve even when its discipline remains intact.
quote_en: “Send us where the battle changes.”

role_en: Use river transport to seize crossings and establish landing points ahead of larger formations.
lore_en: Mekong marines organise their equipment around boats and rapid unloading. Short firearms, boarding blades and poles suit work at banks, landing stages and confined approaches. They secure a foothold before heavier infantry, stores and guns reach the crossing. Their mobility depends on navigable channels and crews who understand them. Once separated from the boats, they fight as light infantry with limited reserves of ammunition and protection.
quote_en: “The road may turn. The river continues.”

role_en: Break disturbed enemy formations and carry shock power into An Nam’s main offensive.
lore_en: War elephants advance under experienced handlers with spears and a modest fighting platform. Their size threatens infantry already shaken by artillery, while the animals’ carrying capacity supports the accompanying assault. Mahouts judge footing, noise and the routes through which an elephant can withdraw safely. These units demand food and careful management; concentrated gunfire or a frightened animal can turn a powerful charge into danger for its own line.
quote_en: “Clear the road before the trumpet.”

role_en: Deliver an elite elephant reserve while protecting high-ranking command groups during battle.
lore_en: Royal elephant guards pair selected animals with disciplined crews and better protection than the ordinary corps. Restrained imperial fittings identify valuable platforms that can carry command staff or support a decisive shock attack. Their handlers practise moving beside regular formations without disordering them. Armour and ceremony add weight, while concentrated fire still threatens the animals. Commanders commit these costly guards where a clear route and prepared support justify their presence.
quote_en: “The imperial standard moves at its own pace.”

role_en: Cross broken uplands and forest routes that deny ordinary cavalry, then strike exposed flanks and communications.
lore_en: Tây Sơn highland riders are recruited from communities accustomed to steep tracks, poor roads and long movement through difficult country. Light horses, compact weapons and minimal baggage let them bypass routes that conventional cavalry considers impractical. Their officers specialise in hidden approaches, ambushes and guiding larger columns through the western uplands. They cannot match heavy cavalry in a frontal collision, but they often arrive from directions the enemy had dismissed as impassable.
quote_en: “The road ends. We keep riding.”

role_en: Exploit darkness and exhaustion to raid camps, horse lines, ammunition wagons and retreat routes before dawn.
lore_en: Dạ Tập cavalry is trained for the hours when an enemy believes marching has ended. Light weapons, quiet tack and disciplined route finding let small detachments circle camps, cut pickets and strike supply points before a larger response forms. Their Vestigium sharpens low-light perception and delays fatigue rather than concealing them outright, allowing riders to fight after a full day’s movement. They remain lightly protected and should disappear before surprise turns into a prolonged battle.
quote_en: “They marched all day. We attack before they sleep.”

role_en: Outmarch enemy cavalry, penetrate deep rear areas and strike communications before defenders believe contact is possible.
lore_en: Bách Lý riders bind a restrained endurance Vestigium to both horse and rider. It steadies breathing, slows muscular exhaustion, improves recovery and delays dehydration, allowing repeated forced marches with far shorter pauses than ordinary cavalry can sustain. The effect does not erase injury or exhaustion; abuse across several days can still ruin mounts and riders. Their doctrine turns distance into surprise, letting them cut couriers, depots and retreat roads long before an opponent expects mounted troops to arrive.
quote_en: “A hundred li is not the journey. It is where the raid begins.”

class_en: Female Vestigium Elephant Guard · Death-Oath Corps
role_en: Guard Nguyễn Huệ and decisive positions with an all-female elephant corps whose Vestigium intensifies with voluntary risk.
lore_en: The Bùi Gia Nữ Tượng Vệ is an all-female veteran order built around elephant warfare, close assault and absolute loyalty to Nguyễn Huệ. Its Vestigium, Quyết Tử Tâm, strengthens when a warrior knowingly accepts greater danger for Nguyễn Huệ or an order entrusted by him: pain tolerance rises, bleeding slows, stamina returns and wounds begin to close fast enough to keep her fighting. The effect rewards conscious sacrifice rather than frenzy and cannot overcome catastrophic injury; cannon shot and mortal wounds still kill. A lesser resonance steadies their elephants under fire, making the corps brutally difficult to stop once committed.
quote_en: “If he still stands, so do we.”

role_en: Concentrate affordable field guns to overwhelm chosen sectors before infantry closes.
lore_en: Mass artillery turns repeatable manufacture into battlefield weight. Practical bronze barrels and simple carriages equip batteries whose crews train around familiar parts and measured charges. Individual guns need not be exceptional when many can fire against the same objective. Officers coordinate ammunition delivery and target selection with the advancing infantry. The system’s weakness is consumption: a rapid offensive can empty powder stocks faster than the workshops replace them.
quote_en: “One gun is ordinary. The battery is not.”

role_en: Move light batteries forward quickly to keep fire support beside the advancing assault.
lore_en: Mobile gun crews trade barrel weight for pace. Compact cannon, economical carriages and trained handling teams allow a battery to follow a breakthrough before defenders establish another line. The crews must choose firm ground and keep routes open for ammunition. Their fire lacks the weight of larger batteries, but timely support can prevent an isolated vanguard from losing the ground it has just taken.
quote_en: “The next position needs its guns now.”

class_en: Elephant Gun Platform · Mobile Heavy Fire
role_en: Carry short heavy guns directly with the elephant corps, combining mobile firepower with close-range shock.
lore_en: Thần Cơ elephant batteries mount compact heavy guns, swivel pieces and reinforced firing frames upon selected war elephants. Gun crews use the animal’s carrying strength to bring grapeshot and heavy close-range fire across ground that would slow conventional carriages, then withdraw or advance with the shock formation. The elephants are specially conditioned for blast and recoil, but concentrated enemy fire can still panic or kill them. Their value lies in moving serious firepower with the assault rather than replacing true siege artillery.
quote_en: “The gun moves because the elephant does.”

role_en: Break a prepared opening through synchronised movement, escalating speed and close-range force.
lore_en: The Tây Sơn Divine Guard takes its name from the western uplands that shaped its martial tradition. Its Vestigium does not burn constantly: each coordinated step, turn and weapon exchange stores motion through body and blade, surfacing as copper-red lines only when force is released. Fighters who keep the cadence gain escalating speed and impact; pin them, break the rhythm or split the formation and the effect decays. The Guard enters after artillery and elephants have opened the line, converting movement into collapse.
quote_en: “One step takes shape. Ten steps become an army. A hundred steps break the line.”

role_en: Concentrate heavy cannon at sea gates and support river-mouth assaults.
lore_en: A broad Vietnamese coastal hull carries a compact battery beneath two battened sails. Provincial yards supply timber and fittings while shore arsenals keep ammunition close. Strong bows and low working decks favour aggressive approaches; shallow estuaries still demand pilots, and open-ocean pursuit strains the crew.
quote_en: “The sea gate opens under our guns.”

role_en: Close through coastal calms and seize disrupted enemy decks.
lore_en: Long oar banks drive this narrow fighting galley independently of the wind. A heavy bow gun opens the approach before boarding bridges carry the assault across. The hull follows Vietnamese galley traditions adapted for coordinated river-sea attacks. Rowers need frequent relief, and high seas can turn its speed into exhaustion.
quote_en: “One drum. One closing stroke.”

role_en: Break defended crossings with concentrated forward artillery.
lore_en: A shallow reinforced hull carries one oversized smoothbore gun on a broad recoil bed. Sweeps and towlines position the boat in narrow channels while its small sail assists longer moves. The compact battery lets An Nam bring siege weight into river combat. Recoil, grounding and limited ammunition demand deliberate shots.
quote_en: “The crossing answers to the muzzle.”

role_en: Locate enemy movements and connect river flotillas with the coastal fleet.
lore_en: A fine narrow hull and light sail plan give Phi Vân speed around headlands. Sweeps carry it through tidal narrows where larger hulls must wait. Local pilots report landings and guide the main squadron toward a useful approach. Light swivel guns deter small raiders; a frigate encounter is a signal to withdraw.
quote_en: “The first sail carries the warning.”

role_en: Move troops, field guns and supplies between rivers and coastal landing grounds.
lore_en: Wide cargo hatches and removable benches turn a local trading hull into organised military lift. Reinforced deck beams carry dismounted gun carriages while smaller boats make the final landing. River-sea interoperability shortens An Nam’s reinforcement routes. Loaded draught rises sharply, and escort is essential when the army packs the holds.
quote_en: “The army arrives with its powder.”

role_en: Drive anchored enemies from constricted water with prepared fire attacks.
lore_en: An expendable shallow boat carries bundled resinous fuel behind a reinforced steering station. Grapnels hold it against a target while an escape skiff carries its crew clear. River-mouth winds and tide govern the attack as closely as courage. A premature ignition or changing current can destroy the craft before contact.
quote_en: “Let the tide carry the spark.”

class_en: River Landing Boat · Rapid Troop Movement
role_en: Carry assault detachments through shallow tributaries and onto exposed banks.
lore_en: A light plank-built hull keeps landing troops close to the water and needs few hands to move. Paddles drive it through reeds, while a removable canopy shelters stores during repeated transfers. These boats sustain An Nam’s rapid tempo by spreading lift across many channels. Low sides and scant protection make surprise more useful than a firefight.
quote_en: “Every stream is another road.”

role_en: Supply the dynasty’s vast infantry mass for garrisons, demonstrations and broad defensive fronts.
lore_en: Provincial banner levies arrive with padded coats, spears and equipment inherited from local stores. Their numbers allow the court to fill roads and defensive lines, while banners help officers keep separate musters identifiable. Training and weapon quality vary between provinces. A well-led contingent can hold useful ground, but distant commands and uneven supplies make a huge muster much harder to turn than its impressive appearance suggests.
quote_en: “Count the banners. Then find the men.”

role_en: Disrupt close approaches with firelances before engaging with the attached spear.
lore_en: Firelance troops preserve a weapon that combines a short burst of flame or shot with a spear shaft. Padded clothing and modest helmets protect crews handling fragile charges near the front. The first discharge can unsettle attackers in confined ground, after which the soldier relies on the point. Short reach, preparation and limited repeat fire prevent the corps from replacing modern musket infantry despite its dramatic appearance.
quote_en: “The first breath is fire. The second is steel.”

role_en: Deliver imported-pattern musket volleys within the dynasty’s uneven reform programme.
lore_en: Celestial musketeers carry firearms acquired or copied from foreign models, paired with Chinese coats and newly adopted cartridge equipment. Selected companies practise ordered firing, giving commanders useful gun infantry when instructors, parts and ammunition are available together. Different arsenals still supply incompatible fittings and habits. Their effectiveness can exceed that of the levies, while hurried expansion spreads trained officers too thin across the court’s many ambitious formations.
quote_en: “The manual is clear. The stores are less so.”

role_en: Protect palace approaches and brace close defensive lines behind large shields.
lore_en: Dragon shield guards carry broad decorated shields over padded or lamellar protection. Their households rehearse guarding gates and moving through ceremonial corridors, producing disciplined close defence in familiar ground. Shields help against arrows and fragments but offer limited security under sustained musket fire. Their visual grandeur makes them a favoured court formation, while weight and restricted visibility punish long advances across an open battlefield.
quote_en: “A palace door has room for very few enemies.”

role_en: Defend the imperial household with selected halberdiers and concentrated polearm reach.
lore_en: Golden dragon halberdiers display the court’s finest polearms and gilded armour fittings. Their formation keeps enemies away from important persons and offers strong close control at entrances or around a command enclosure. Ceremony preserves discipline but also adds cumbersome ornament. Officers who treat their appearance as proof of universal superiority discover the limits of heavily equipped foot guards under artillery and fast-changing field conditions.
quote_en: “Gold marks the post. Steel keeps it.”

role_en: Attack disturbed enemy infantry with selected sword companies carrying heavy dao blades.
lore_en: White tiger swordsmen represent the court’s preference for named assault corps with recognisable dress and martial prestige. Padded white-grey coats and strong dao swords equip soldiers trained to close after supporting missiles unsettle a target. Good companies can exploit a local collapse with force. Their reputation tempts commanders into exposed frontal attacks, where ornament and individual swordsmanship offer little answer to coordinated gunfire.
quote_en: “The tiger still needs a path to its prey.”

role_en: Threaten exposed stores and crowded approaches with coordinated incendiary arrow volleys.
lore_en: Fire-arrow battalions carry bows and carefully stored ignition materials for attacks on vulnerable structures and supplies. Their effect depends on choosing targets that can burn and reaching a position from which enough arrows land together. Damp conditions and hurried preparation spoil the result. They supplement other missile formations, while the court’s enthusiasm for flame often exceeds the modest battlefield value of poorly aimed incendiaries.
quote_en: “Choose what can burn before lighting the arrow.”

role_en: Provide massed bolt fire from prepared defensive positions with maintained crossbows.
lore_en: Imperial crossbow regiments retain familiar mechanisms and bolt stores where firearm reform remains incomplete. Their companies can prepare measured volleys without consuming gunpowder, making them useful for defended approaches and supporting large musters. Loading equipment and ammunition remain substantial burdens. They struggle when mobile opponents dictate the distance, and heavy armour or modern gunfire reduces the comfort of relying on an older missile arm.
quote_en: “Every bolt has a place in the rack.”

role_en: Supply garrisons with older matchlock fire where newer weapons remain scarce.
lore_en: Ming arquebusiers guard magazines and fort approaches with primitive firearms distributed from older arsenals. Long tunics, powder flasks and simple bandoliers reflect gradual acquisition rather than uniform modernisation. Their knowledge of a fixed position helps compensate for slow loading and uncertain maintenance. They can strengthen a prepared defence, but damp matches and incompatible powder charges make a hurried march followed by immediate firing a difficult assignment.
quote_en: “The match must live before the gun speaks.”

role_en: Prepare siege approaches and maintain the dynasty’s cumbersome war machinery.
lore_en: Imperial engineers carry measuring rods and carpentry tools among the army’s many experimental devices. They build supports, repair wheels and prepare approaches that ceremonial formations often overlook. Their practical experience can make a copied weapon usable or reveal that an ambitious design lacks a workable transport plan. Workshops compete for imperial favour, leaving the corps to manage incompatible parts and machinery whose appearance sometimes outpaces its reliability.
quote_en: “A drawing cannot carry its own weight.”

role_en: Test imported tactical systems while providing selected infantry with borrowed weapons and drill.
lore_en: Foreign-pattern regiments display the dynasty’s urge to acquire every successful method. Chinese garments meet imported straps, firearms and marching routines, often assembled from several foreign examples. Some companies learn enough to become effective experiments; others receive new equipment faster than experienced instructors. Their commanders must simplify conflicting manuals into usable orders. Success depends on adapting a coherent system rather than accumulating impressive fragments of several.
quote_en: “Choose one command before giving three.”

role_en: Provide the court’s grand reserve through a vast muster of selected provincial contingents.
lore_en: The ten thousand banners guard gathers prestigious companies beneath imperial authority, creating a reserve whose visible scale can reassure allies and intimidate opponents. Equipment ranges from fine guard armour to respectable provincial kit. Separate contingents preserve their own drill and officers, complicating a sudden common manoeuvre. The formation becomes useful when deployed in manageable bodies; committing the whole spectacle at once can turn numerical strength into confusion.
quote_en: “The banners fill the field. Orders must cross it.”

role_en: Redeploy firearm detachments by horse, then fight from chosen dismounted positions.
lore_en: Heavenly dragoons imitate a foreign military function more successfully when officers remember to separate travel from firing. Horses move musketeers between threatened points; the men dismount to form a useful line. Mixed riding equipment and firearm patterns complicate training and supply. A capable detachment can reinforce a flank quickly, while poorly drilled imitators arrive as riders who struggle to become infantry when the order changes.
quote_en: “Ride to the order. Stand to the shot.”

role_en: Deliver lance shock against weakened formations with heavily equipped imperial cavalry.
lore_en: Dragon lancers combine armoured riders, decorated horse fittings and long lances into an imposing charge. Good horses and adequate drill give them real striking power against a line already disturbed by artillery or missiles. Their mass requires space and a coherent approach. Courtly display can encourage premature commitment, leaving costly cavalry trapped against prepared points or firing lines before its impact can matter.
quote_en: “The charge needs more than a magnificent horse.”

role_en: Screen the dynasty’s frontier columns through mobile archery and local riding experience.
lore_en: Border horse archers carry composite bows, quivers and practical riding clothes shaped by northern service. Their flexible groups observe approaches and harass opponents without the burdens of elaborate palace cavalry. They are valuable wherever frontier experience survives administrative distance from the court. Ammunition and healthy horses limit prolonged operations, while attempts to force these riders into ceremonial mass charges waste their ability to choose distance.
quote_en: “The frontier teaches before the court names.”

role_en: Disturb concentrated troops and supply areas with massed unguided rocket fire.
lore_en: Thunderclap crews prepare clusters of period rocket tubes on simple wooden racks. Their projectiles deliver smoke, noise and scattered impact across a broad sector, forcing enemies to disperse or interrupt an approach. Powder variation and wind make precision unreliable. Careful crews separate stores from launch points and keep escorts nearby. The court admires the spectacle; field officers value the temporary disorder it can create.
quote_en: “The noise arrives together. The arrows do not.”

role_en: Support imperial infantry with conventional field cannon from the dynasty’s varied arsenals.
lore_en: Mandarin artillery officers oversee batteries whose barrels and carriages can differ greatly between workshops. Capable crews measure charges, prepare stable ground and protect powder, giving the army dependable fire when those routines are respected. Administrators often prioritise inspection and appearance alongside readiness. The corps’ chief problem is coordination: many guns can be present while ammunition, draft teams and useful targets fail to arrive together.
quote_en: “A cannon on the list still needs powder.”

role_en: Breach fixed defences with the dynasty’s largest and most cumbersome siege guns.
lore_en: The great dragon bombard announces imperial commitment through barrel weight, ornament and an extraordinary transport train. Crews must construct firm firing beds and organise enough powder and shot for the siege to justify its arrival. Its impact against fixed works can be severe. Yet a vast cannon offers little flexibility once the enemy moves elsewhere, turning courtly ambition into a problem of roads, labour and time.
quote_en: “The emperor ordered the gun. The road must obey.”

role_en: Drop incendiary charges from primitive fire balloons when weather and preparation permit.
lore_en: Fire-balloon crews assemble fabric envelopes, bamboo baskets and early lifting arrangements for an ambitious aerial weapon. Prepared charges threaten stationary targets beneath a favourable drift. The system depends on wind, lift and a launch site with room to work, making precise targeting uncertain. Court observers see an image of celestial power; the operators must judge whether the same breeze will carry the weapon toward the enemy or their own stores.
quote_en: “The sky has received no imperial orders.”

role_en: Protect balloon launch sites and keep lifting equipment under control during preparation.
lore_en: Balloon guards combine spear escorts with rope handlers, anchor crews and workers who secure the launch area. They clear space around powder and fabric, prevent interference and manage the lines while operators prepare the envelope. Their role is essential to an unpredictable weapon with a vulnerable ground footprint. Once a balloon departs, the detachment remains ordinary light infantry around bulky stores, requiring support against a determined field attack.
quote_en: “Hold the rope until the order.”

class_en: Immortal Vestigium Order · One Hundred and Eight Heroes
role_en: Destroy elite formations and command centres through 108 ageless champions held permanently at physical prime.
lore_en: The order is composed of the same one hundred and eight named heroes of Liangshan: thirty-six Heavenly Spirits and seventy-two Earthly Fiends. Vestigium arrested their ageing at physical prime without making them impossible to kill; each remains the person preserved in the classical tale, with original temperament, relationships and martial identity intact. Their weapons blaze with brilliant golden Vestigium, magnifying strength, speed, endurance and impact rather than granting mutable supernatural forms. They cannot be reproduced, replaced or trained anew.
quote_en: “One hundred and eight names. None have grown old.”

role_en: Anchor coastal squadrons with a broad, durable gun platform.
lore_en: Hai Long carries massed crews behind high timber bulwarks and a broad battened rig. A reinforced working deck supports numerous conventional cannon without machinery. Its impressive bulk suits coastal control, but ammunition handling and signals become difficult when court-appointed officers compete for authority.
quote_en: “A thousand hands hold the sea.”

role_en: Dominate close coastal fighting from elevated command and missile positions.
lore_en: An upper fighting gallery rises over a stout river-capable hull. Archers and matchlock troops cover grappling parties while low-mounted guns keep recoil near the water. Tower height communicates imperial strength and aids observation. It also catches wind, loads the topweight and makes rough-water service hazardous.
quote_en: “The banner sees beyond the wall.”

role_en: Concentrate heavy smoothbore fire against defended sea gates.
lore_en: A short broad hull trades cargo space for strengthened gun beds and shot lockers. Arsenal cannon are grouped for deliberate attacks from surveyed positions. This vessel gives the dynasty a specialist battery without making every junk a siege ship. Slow turns and deep loaded draught require escorts and reliable channel marks.
quote_en: “The gate has heard our summons.”

role_en: Watch fishing approaches and intercept light coastal raiders.
lore_en: Fine hull lines and a manageable sail plan let patrol crews spend more days underway than parade ships. Light cannon and sweeps suit inspection, pursuit and sheltered-water intervention. Its officers work with fishing communities to distinguish ordinary traffic from invasion scouts. Limited provisions restrict independent ocean patrols.
quote_en: “The quiet sail is counted too.”

role_en: Break anchored concentrations through controlled fire-attack approaches.
lore_en: A stripped expendable hull carries fuel baskets, ignition pots and grapnels. Towing boats position it before the crew sets a timed escape. Mass attacks can overwhelm a crowded anchorage, but wind and coordination determine whether fire reaches the enemy. Powder stores are limited to reduce the danger before release.
quote_en: “One drifting hull scatters a hundred.”

role_en: Direct large flotillas through clear signals and protected staff work.
lore_en: A raised stern platform carries drums, signal racks and sheltered charts. The hull retains a useful defensive battery while its spacious deck gathers pilots and liaison officers. Imperial spectacle is made operational through recognisable banners. Losing the flagship or obscuring its signals can leave the vast fleet acting as separate boats.
quote_en: “Watch the centre banner.”

role_en: Carry the dynasty’s authority into major coastal assemblies.
lore_en: Tian Wei uses selected treasure-voyage influences in its high stern, generous hull and ceremonial rig. Imported fine timber and court craftsmen make it a visible statement of imperial reach. Its cannon and guards can defend the royal party, yet costly fittings and extensive service staff reduce combat efficiency. Admirals escort it rather than risk the court’s symbol casually.
quote_en: “The court has reached the water.”

role_en: Protect the sultan and counterattack threatened gateways with selected household infantry.
lore_en: The household guard combines fine mail, patterned cloth and well-made blades with the discipline of permanent court service. Its soldiers are strongest around defended entrances and nearby reserves, where officers know the approaches and can commit a compact force at the right moment. Royal status secures better equipment but limits numbers. Distant campaigning removes the familiar ground and local support that help these guards protect the sultanate.
quote_en: “The threshold belongs to the sultan.”

role_en: Hold palace districts and fortified settlements with organised Javanese garrison infantry.
lore_en: Prajurit Keraton maintain the watches, armouries and access points on which the palace depends. Spears, shields and regional cloth identify infantry accustomed to clear duties within a defended settlement. Their routine keeps troops ready when coastal alarms reach the interior. They support field forces by securing stores and command centres, although long expeditions demand scouting and supply habits beyond the familiar rhythm of garrison service.
quote_en: “Every gate has its watch.”

role_en: Defend coastal settlements and delay enemy landings through local militia resistance.
lore_en: Laskar Pesisir muster around inlets, landing grounds and defended villages.
