Old firearms, spears and practical clothing vary with local resources, while knowledge of paths and supply caches helps fighters return after a setback. They are useful at denying an invader an easy first foothold. Their strength declines away from home, where uneven drill and equipment make coordination harder and the local support network can no longer sustain them.
quote_en: “The inlet has more defenders than houses.”

role_en: Ambush invading columns along narrow forest approaches and withdraw before formed retaliation.
lore_en: Jungle raiders use muted cloth, compact blades and light missile weapons to remain mobile through close vegetation. Small groups watch paths and strike where a column cannot bring its full strength to bear. They depend on local guides, concealed stores and a safe route away from the attack. Their success can delay an invasion without winning a conventional battle, while distant open-ground campaigning deprives them of their best advantages.
quote_en: “A long column has many lonely men.”

role_en: Find concealed movement and guide allied troops through difficult forest routes.
lore_en: Dayak scouts contribute regional knowledge within the sultanate’s defensive coalition. Light clothing, compact cutting tools and local missile weapons suit patient observation and movement through narrow paths. They report crossings and concealed approaches before heavier infantry enters the area. Allied commanders gain valuable reconnaissance by allowing them independent judgement; large formations, unfamiliar terrain and compulsory line duty reduce the usefulness of their specialised experience.
quote_en: “The path was used before dawn.”

role_en: Strengthen coastal positions with measured matchlock fire from familiar defended approaches.
lore_en: Acehnese matchlock companies protect harbours and nearby routes with long firearms, powder flasks and practical layered dress. They choose covered positions where slow loading matters less and local stores can keep matches and powder usable. Their volleys support spearmen rather than replacing them. An army trying to carry these companies far overseas must provide the maintenance and supply routines that home garrisons normally obtain from their settlements.
quote_en: “Keep the powder dry behind the wall.”

role_en: Brace protected approaches and screen gun crews with disciplined Javanese spear infantry.
lore_en: Java spear guards maintain ordered points around gateways, road junctions and firing positions. Practical shields and modest protection allow resources to be concentrated on durable weapons and drill. They work with matchlock companies, closing the space an attacker would exploit between volleys. Their defence depends on cohesion and selected ground; artillery and broad manoeuvre can make a steady spear line irrelevant before it meets an enemy.
quote_en: “Let the gunners finish their loading.”

role_en: Resolve close encounters around obstacles with experienced kris-bearing blade infantry.
lore_en: Kris veterans carry distinctive sidearms beside practical longer blades, keeping familiar martial traditions within a field formation. Fine patterned cloth and selected protection mark experienced fighters assigned to entrances and short approaches. Their skill matters after the enemy has been drawn into a confined contest. Exposed advances against prepared musket fire remain costly, so commanders use guides and supporting missiles to bring the veterans into useful contact.
quote_en: “The narrow place remembers our steps.”

role_en: Raid shipping and seize confined shipboard access through experienced Bugis assault groups.
lore_en: Bugis sea raiders carry compact blades, short firearms and little baggage for movement between boats and hostile decks. Their experience favours a fast approach and a clear objective, followed by withdrawal or consolidation before defenders concentrate. Sea transport extends their reach around the archipelago. Large inland campaigns require a different support system, while exposed approaches against an alert warship can destroy a lightly protected boarding party.
quote_en: “A rail is only another threshold.”

role_en: Secure ports and contest enemy landings with organised Makassar naval infantry.
lore_en: Makassar marines combine maritime familiarity with the steadiness needed to remain after a raid ends. Firearms, spears and boarding blades support defence around quays, warehouses and landing stages. They protect the movement of crews and stores while the sultanate’s boats reinforce a threatened shore. Their equipment suits confined ground and local transport, with less striking power when a distant campaign forces them into prolonged open-field warfare.
quote_en: “The boats need somewhere safe to return.”

role_en: Move troops and messages along waterways to outpace invaders restricted to inland paths.
lore_en: River-canoe detachments carry paddles, compact weapons and small loads organised for rapid embarkation. Familiar crews can shift fighters between threatened points and secure crossings before a marching column arrives. Their knowledge of channels is as important as their personal arms. Shallow water, blocked landings and enemy guns can interrupt the system, leaving transported troops with limited protection and little capacity for a long independent march.
quote_en: “The water reaches the other post first.”

role_en: Reach threatened points quickly, reinforce shaken detachments and punish raiders before they vanish into jungle-edge routes.
lore_en: The sultanates cannot always wait for infantry to arrive on foot, especially when ports, depots or inland roads are struck suddenly. Rapid Response Cavalry exists as a compact mounted reserve, dispatched to seal gaps, reinforce local commanders and chase off disruptive raids before they become larger crises. Their doctrine is practical, defensive and time-sensitive rather than aristocratic.
quote_en: “We arrive where delay becomes defeat.”

role_en: Scout inland routes, watch approaches and guide columns between settlements, river paths and coastal roads.
lore_en: Large cavalry formations do not define Nusantara warfare, but mounted scouts still have real utility wherever speed matters more than weight. Peninjau Berkuda use light horses and practical equipment to report enemy movement, test routes and connect dispersed commanders across difficult island terrain. Their value lies in mobility and local knowledge, not in grand mounted charges.
quote_en: “The road is safer when someone reaches it first.”

role_en: Deny defended harbours and approaches with cannon served from permanent fort positions.
lore_en: Benteng crews know their embrasures, ammunition rooms and firing distances through repeated watches. Bronze or iron pieces can strike landing craft and troops before an invasion establishes secure stores ashore. Walls protect the crews while local workshops maintain carriages and tools. Their power remains tied to prepared positions; a successful landing elsewhere can bypass a formidable gun that lacks transport or troops to defend its rear.
quote_en: “We measured this water before your sails arrived.”

role_en: Support local counterattacks with light guns that can move between defended approaches.
lore_en: Sultanate field gunners employ compact cannon and simple carriages suited to short relocations around home territory. Crews follow prepared paths and draw ammunition from nearby settlements, reinforcing the point an invader has chosen to press. Their pieces favour timely support over enormous shot weight. Difficult ground and limited draft teams constrain movement, while distant expeditions remove the local knowledge and stores on which the batteries rely.
quote_en: “The next inlet needs this gun.”

class_en: Sultanate Forest Trackers · Deep Jungle Hunters
role_en: Track raiders, monsters, infiltrators and Vestigium disturbances through terrain hostile to conventional pursuit.
lore_en: The Trackers are drawn from people for whom forest movement is a practiced craft rather than an obstacle. They read broken vegetation, water movement, animal silence and abandoned camps to follow targets that believe the jungle has hidden them. Small units may remain detached for days while larger forces wait for the one signal that tells them where to strike.
quote_en: “The forest speaks before the fugitive does.”

role_en: Eliminate officers, infiltrators and dangerous specialists in terrain where formations and long firearms lose their advantage.
lore_en: The Black Keris Pendekar work in streets, palace compounds, jungle paths and ship interiors where battle collapses into seconds of close violence. Their keris are tools of identity as much as weapons, paired with pistols, climbing equipment and patient observation. They avoid open battle whenever possible because their value lies in reaching one person the army cannot.
quote_en: “One corridor is enough.”

role_en: Shield inter-island convoys with a durable fighting hull.
lore_en: A deep rounded Javanese-derived hull carries layered timber sides and a broad cargo deck. Tanja sails move its weight between island arsenals while defensive cannon protect valuable traffic. The sultanate uses it as a mobile convoy strongpoint. Deep draught keeps it outside the reef channels where lighter local craft excel.
quote_en: “The cargo sails behind a wall.”

role_en: Rush through tidal narrows and reinforce threatened shores.
lore_en: A shallow long hull combines oar banks with a modest local rig. Bow cannon clear the approach while a broad landing platform carries assault stores. Lancaran crews exploit currents and familiar straits to arrive before an invading column consolidates. Sustained rowing consumes manpower that the same expedition needs ashore.
quote_en: “The strait gives us the hour.”

role_en: Strike isolated boats and withdraw through shallow inlets.
lore_en: A fine narrow hull keeps the raider quick and difficult to follow. Paddles and a light sail complement a few swivel guns and concealed grapnels. Local crews choose reef passages that frustrate deep-draught escorts. Thin planking and small magazines make every prolonged exchange costly.
quote_en: “The inlet closes behind us.”

role_en: Bring a concentrated forward battery against harbour approaches.
lore_en: Regional builders adapt a stout ghurab hull to carry heavier bow guns and reinforced recoil beds. Its rig reflects Indian Ocean exchange, while local timber work and fittings retain the sultanate’s identity. Escorts cover the flanks as it attacks a selected approach. Heavy ammunition reduces endurance and useful cargo space.
quote_en: “The harbour hears the bow first.”

role_en: Lead oared assault groups and coordinate decisive boarding attacks.
lore_en: A long galley hull carries a protected command canopy over disciplined oar crews. Regional gun founders supply bow cannon and light deck pieces. The royal banner gathers fast boats for a concentrated attack rather than a scattered chase. Elaborate fittings and a large crew make this prestige craft expensive to sustain.
quote_en: “Every oar follows the banner.”

role_en: Carry warnings between ports and inspect hidden coastal approaches.
lore_en: A light shallow hull can be hauled onto beaches for quick repair. Small sails and paddles keep messenger routes open through calms and narrow water. Its crew combines reconnaissance with liaison between local defenders. A handful of swivel guns provides warning shots, leaving heavy fighting to the flotilla.
quote_en: “The next island must know.”

role_en: Carry troops and provisions between dispersed island commitments.
lore_en: A capacious local sailing hull retains merchant construction while adding troop benches and secured weapon stores. Smaller landing craft make the last approach to reef-fringed shores. The ship sustains island defence by moving organised loads across the archipelago. Monsoon timing and loaded draught govern its sailing schedule.
quote_en: “The island holds because the stores arrive.”

role_en: Form a modern musket line under Tokugawa authority using adapted Western drill.
lore_en: Tokugawa line infantry wears military tailoring redesigned around flintlocks, cartridge belts and common commands. Restrained household emblems preserve political identity within a professional formation. French operational ideas and Company-style training favour reliable movement between volleys, with officers expected to coordinate supporting arms. The system demands maintained arsenals and trained instructors. Its strength lies in repeating a coherent method across regiments rather than relying on the personal prowess of a few swordsmen.
quote_en: “The crest remains. The drill has changed.”

role_en: Concentrate dependable musket fire to support the empire’s coordinated infantry advances.
lore_en: Imperial fusiliers receive carefully maintained flintlocks and standard cartridge equipment through the reformed arsenals. Their companies train to shift fire and maintain intervals as nearby formations move. Practical blue-grey tailoring distinguishes professional field service from household ceremony. High firepower depends on ammunition arriving at the planned pace; prolonged action without resupply consumes the advantage that good weapons and disciplined loading were intended to provide.
quote_en: “A volley is a promise kept together.”

role_en: Clear defended entrances and lead short assaults with trained grenade detachments.
lore_en: Edo grenadiers adapt an imported battlefield role to the empire’s own uniforms and command practices. Grenade pouches, robust firearms and compact tools equip soldiers who rehearse approaching obstacles under covering fire. Their assault teams are committed to a specific breach rather than scattered across the front. The corps depends on reliable fuzes, ammunition and experienced leaders, making careless use of its explosives or veterans an expensive failure.
quote_en: “Clear the entrance. Keep the order.”

role_en: Defend Tokugawa command and restore threatened positions with selected household guards.
lore_en: The shogunal guard pairs household loyalty with training drawn from the reformed army. Fine steel or lacquer protection worn over military coats gives the unit an elite silhouette while firearms keep it useful beyond ceremonial sword duty. Officers hold these soldiers near important command points and contested gateways. Their disciplined counterattack can recover a local crisis, but limited numbers make them too valuable for routine attrition.
quote_en: “The household stands behind the command.”

role_en: Expand the army’s trained infantry base through standard equipment and repeatable firearm drill.
lore_en: Reformed ashigaru companies receive modest uniforms, standard flintlocks and clear regimental routines. Their strength is broad recruitment turned into dependable soldiers through training and maintained stores. They hold ground, support the professional fusiliers and keep the empire’s growing army from depending solely on elite households. Inexperienced officers and rapid expansion can strain the system, so consistent drill matters more than impressive equipment issued without instruction.
quote_en: “An ordinary soldier can learn an excellent method.”

role_en: Screen the main line with mobile light infantry influenced by French reconnaissance and skirmish practice.
lore_en: Japanese chasseurs lighten their equipment and reduce bright fittings for work ahead of the reformed army. Accurate individual fire and observation support the regular line by identifying enemy positions and disrupting exposed troops. Their groups practise independent movement without losing contact with command. They remain vulnerable to determined close assault, requiring a safe route back to formed infantry when reconnaissance becomes a sustained engagement.
quote_en: “The main line should arrive informed.”

role_en: Build, inspect and repair the works that let the reformed army manoeuvre and hold ground.
lore_en: Tokugawa engineers join measuring instruments and practical tools to military field discipline. They prepare crossings, assess fortifications and repair the gun routes on which coordinated offensives depend. Their work carries reform into the ground itself, allowing infantry and batteries to use the same plan. Small detachments are easily disrupted while working; escorts and clear priorities keep technical skill from being consumed by every minor repair request.
quote_en: “An army needs a place to put its method.”

role_en: Force or restore the decisive point with the most disciplined infantry of the reformed army.
lore_en: The shogun’s modern guard joins household loyalty to the best training and equipment available through reform. Refined protection, excellent flintlocks and carefully fitted uniforms reflect a force expected to carry demanding orders without confusion. Its soldiers can stabilise a threatened line or exploit a prepared opening. Their true distinction is coordinated judgement under pressure, while scarce experienced recruits keep the formation a reserve rather than a universal solution.
quote_en: “The newest method serves the oldest oath.”

role_en: Add disciplined Korean musket companies to the imperial line and reinforce sustained firearm engagements.
lore_en: Joseon P’osu regiments were retained after the conquest of Korea because the empire needed trained gunmen more than it needed another ceremonial trophy. Korean officers preserve much of their own firearm drill beneath Japanese operational command, giving these companies dependable volley discipline and strong defensive fire. Their equipment is increasingly standardised through imperial arsenals, although language, loyalty and occupation politics complicate integration. Used well, they deepen the line without becoming a copy of Japanese infantry.
quote_en: “The empire changed the banner. It did not teach us how to shoot.”

class_en: Korean Auxiliary Archers · Mountain Missile Infantry
role_en: Provide precise missile fire, counter-skirmishing and mountain support with experienced Korean archers.
lore_en: Joseon Sasu preserve Korea’s strong military archery within the imperial order. Composite bows, disciplined range judgement and familiarity with steep country make them valuable where smoke, broken ground or limited ammunition reduce the advantage of firearms. Japanese commanders use them as mountain screens, counter-skirmishers and precision missile troops rather than trying to force them into a musket line. Their effectiveness falls in prolonged close combat, where lighter equipment gives little margin for error.
quote_en: “A mountain gives the arrow more places to disappear.”

class_en: Korean Auxiliary Assault Infantry · Spear & Blade
role_en: Protect Korean firearm units and contest broken ground through disciplined spear, blade and polearm fighting.
lore_en: Joseon Salsu companies preserve the close-combat arm of Korea’s mixed military system. Spears, swords and polearms let them guard musketeers, clear narrow approaches and fight effectively where a firing line loses room to work. They are especially useful in villages, passes and fort entrances, where disciplined reach matters more than fashionable equipment. Against heavy modern infantry in open ground, however, courage and technique cannot fully compensate for limited protection.
quote_en: “When the gun line runs out of room, give us the doorway.”

role_en: Establish disciplined landing points and contest shipboard access with modern naval infantry.
lore_en: Japanese marines adapt professional musket drill to quays, boats and crowded decks. Shorter practical coats, boarding tools and secured ammunition support the transition from sea transport to a defensible foothold. They coordinate with ship guns and engineers as stores come ashore. Their value is greatest around the fleet; sustained inland operations require reinforcement and supply beyond the compact loads carried into the first landing.
quote_en: “Secure the shore before unloading the army.”

role_en: Move firearm troops quickly between threatened points and fight from selected dismounted positions.
lore_en: Imperial dragoons combine trained riders with the drill needed to become useful infantry after dismounting. Carbines, swords and compact cartridge equipment keep the mounted load manageable. They reinforce flanks, secure roads and reach ground before slower regiments. Their method demands enough men to handle horses during firing, while poor footing or exhausted mounts can prevent the rapid transfer for which the unit was assembled.
quote_en: “The horse carries the soldier to his firing line.”

role_en: Provide a mobile household reserve for command protection and decisive mounted action.
lore_en: Restored hatamoto retain elite riding traditions within an army whose main strength is increasingly firearm infantry. Selected horses, refined protection and swords or pistols suit escort work and a carefully chosen counterattack. Their role connects household prestige with practical battlefield service. Officers avoid wasting these riders against unbroken bayonets, reserving their mobility for exposed flanks, disrupted formations or a command group that urgently needs protection.
quote_en: “The household rides where it is needed.”

role_en: Provide coordinated field cannon support for the reformed infantry’s advance and defence.
lore_en: Bakufu artillery uses maintained barrels, organised carriages and trained crews influenced by Western practice. Gunners coordinate measured fire with infantry movement, choosing targets that open an approach or interrupt an enemy concentration. Standard stores simplify repair and loading across batteries. Good roads and draft teams remain necessary, while ammunition consumption can outpace even a professional system during a rapid offensive.
quote_en: “Fire where the infantry will need the opening.”

role_en: Reduce defended works with heavy cannon served from carefully prepared siege positions.
lore_en: Heavy siege batteries represent a deliberate commitment of transport, workshops and powder. Their crews establish solid firing beds and organise repair stores before working against walls and fixed guns. Reformed procedures improve reliability without removing the burden of enormous barrels and carriages. These batteries are powerful against a stationary objective, yet vulnerable to a campaign that suddenly demands movement instead of sustained preparation.
quote_en: “The siege begins with the road.”

role_en: Guard the empire’s coastal approaches with prepared guns and trained shore detachments.
lore_en: Pacific coastal guards maintain harbour weapons and watch the routes through which an expedition must approach. Familiar firing distances and nearby stores make their cannon formidable around selected ports. Infantry detachments protect the crews and access roads behind the batteries. This defence remains strongest where the guns are placed; a dispersed coastline forces commanders to balance impressive fixed positions against the need for mobile reserves.
quote_en: “A coast is longer than any wall.”

role_en: Direct reformed formations through experienced samurai officers trained in modern combined operations.
lore_en: Samurai officers carry paired swords as signs of office beside practical firearms and field equipment. Their professional task now includes interpreting reports, coordinating infantry and artillery, and keeping orders clear under disruption. Fine tailoring and selected armour mark authority without requiring a separate way of war for every household. An officer who mistakes inherited status for tactical judgement can still ruin a well-equipped regiment.
quote_en: “The sword marks my duty. The order fulfils it.”

class_en: Crimson Vestigium Vanguard · Hikone Reform Elite
role_en: Break elite opposition through a crimson samurai-reform vanguard whose Vestigium binds armour, weapons and formation into a single shock rhythm.
lore_en: The Ii Red Armour preserves the terrifying visual identity associated with Naomasa’s house, but the modern corps wears crimson lacquer over reform-cut military tunics, cartridge gear and polished field boots. Katana and flintlock arms are tuned to the same Vestigium resonance carried through armour fittings and formation drill. When red remains beside red, nearby warriors reinforce one another’s reactions, stamina and resistance to shock; thin crimson energy crawls along blades, barrels and plate seams as the line accelerates with unnatural unity. Break the formation into isolated pockets and the shared advantage fades rapidly.
quote_en: “So long as red remains beside red, the line still lives.”

role_en: Hold collapsing routes, kill pursuit leaders and buy the army time through masters who alternate a Vestigium handcannon with elite katana work.
lore_en: Shimazu rearguards preserve the ruthless logic of sutegamari: selected hero-masters remain behind while the main force disengages, turning pursuit into deliberate killing points. Each carries an exceptional katana and a Vestigium handcannon whose Last Ember forms its own shot, fires with white-orange force, then lies inert for roughly fifteen seconds. During that interval the wielder returns to the blade. Isolation sharpens perception, pain tolerance and close-combat reaction; the effect rewards disciplined sacrifice and fades when the survivor rejoins the main force.
quote_en: “Go. We will decide how many of them follow.”

class_en: Ship of the Line · Battle Squadron
role_en: Provide disciplined heavy broadside combat for the modernised fleet.
lore_en: French-informed hull calculations shape a Japanese-built two-decker with carefully spaced gun ports. Local yards preserve restrained lacquer work and Tokugawa crests while adopting common shot sizes and sailing drills. Its strong battery anchors a conventional battle squadron. Timber, trained crews and large dock facilities limit the number Japan can maintain.
quote_en: “The old banner commands both decks.”

role_en: Defeat ordinary escorts and guard the battle squadron’s approaches.
lore_en: A long hull supports one covered battery with heavy conventional guns. French sailing practice informs rig balance and coordinated manoeuvre, while Japanese carpenters build fittings for domestic maintenance. The frigate can fight hard without a capital ship’s expense. Its single gun deck still leaves it vulnerable in a line engagement.
quote_en: “The current carries a steady gun.”

role_en: Run down raiders and preserve contact with retreating enemies.
lore_en: Fine entry lines and generous canvas trade some broadside weight for speed. Japanese officers apply imported rig-handling methods to a service culture that prizes prompt execution. Chase guns open an interception before the main battery bears. Light framing and a demanding sail plan make rough weather and damage costly.
quote_en: “Keep the fleeing sail in sight.”

role_en: Escort smaller convoys and patrol distant imperial stations.
lore_en: A compact corvette carries a modest battery under a manageable square rig. French-inspired arrangement improves access to stores and simplifies watch routines. Korean and Japanese ports supply pilots and repairs across the empire’s coastal routes. Limited magazine capacity rewards careful escort work rather than prolonged squadron combat.
quote_en: “A small escort keeps a long promise.”

role_en: Hold harbour approaches with heavy forward fire.
lore_en: A broad low hull carries a reinforced bow battery and short auxiliary rig. Imported artillery doctrine helps crews lay measured fire across surveyed channels. Japanese yards retain local shallow-water handling and practical fittings. The vessel defends a prepared approach efficiently, but exposed open-water pursuit defeats its purpose.
quote_en: “The harbour has measured this shot.”

role_en: Carry orders and reconnaissance reports between separated squadrons.
lore_en: A narrow two-masted schooner uses imported fore-and-aft sailing methods with locally made spars and fittings. Secure document chests and clear signal stations take priority over guns. It lets Japanese admirals coordinate ships beyond sight of the flagship. Weather, fatigue and scant defensive fire limit independent work in hostile water.
quote_en: “The order reaches the next horizon.”

role_en: Test auxiliary steam while directing selected modern squadrons.
lore_en: Tenkai combines a French-informed wooden hull with an imported auxiliary engine and locally adapted command spaces. Sail remains the main means of passage; steam secures station during calms and difficult approaches. Limited plating protects the machinery rather than turning the whole fleet into ironclads. Coal, spare parts and scarce engineers keep this experiment exceptional.
quote_en: “The new engine serves the old banner.”

role_en: Hold camps, wagons, crossings and constrained ground where cavalry cannot deploy freely.
lore_en: The Great Khanate is remembered for its riders, but even a horse empire needs men on foot. Steppe Infantry are drawn from camp retainers, poorer clansmen and dismounted attendants who defend baggage, secure camps and fight in rough ground unsuited to mounted action. They lack the prestige of the cavalry hosts, yet many mounted victories survive only because these foot soldiers keep the army’s rear, supplies and narrow approaches intact.
quote_en: “Not every victory is won from the saddle.”

role_en: Harass enemy formations with mobile bow fire while preserving distance and freedom of movement.
lore_en: Steppe horse archers carry composite bows and deep quivers on hardy mounts. Their groups approach, loose and disengage around a shared understanding of pace and space. They force foot armies to watch several directions while revealing openings for heavier riders. Their endurance depends on remounts, forage and arrows. Confined ground or a defended crossing can remove the freedom that makes a lightly protected horse archer dangerous.
quote_en: “The target stands. The bow keeps moving.”

role_en: Deliver concentrated mounted shock after lighter riders expose a vulnerable enemy sector.
lore_en: The khan’s heavy lancers combine selected horses, lamellar protection and long lances for a decisive impact. They wait while scouts and archers identify an angle that avoids the enemy’s strongest points. Weight gives their charge power but also raises the cost of transport and horse care. They are a reserve for a favourable collision, with little benefit in repeated attacks against unbroken gun lines.
quote_en: “Find the opening. Then lower the lance.”

role_en: Strike deep supply routes and force opponents to divide their marching forces.
lore_en: Tumen raiders carry minimal baggage and enough weapons for several short encounters. Their groups move around the main field army, targeting stores, couriers and isolated detachments before withdrawing across open country. Commanders value disruption more than possession of every attacked place. The raid system relies on information and fresh horses; poor reconnaissance or terrain that blocks escape can trap a force whose protection was sacrificed for speed.
quote_en: “The army marches where its food can follow.”

role_en: Screen the khanate’s columns and report enemy routes through far-ranging mounted observation.
lore_en: Skyward scouts ride ahead and around the army with light bows, compact tools and little ceremonial equipment. They identify crossings, enemy concentrations and available forage before the main force commits. Their reports connect speed to a useful destination. Scouts avoid being fixed in prolonged fighting, since a lost messenger can be more damaging than a missed skirmish. Their reach contracts sharply in dense or enclosed country.
quote_en: “The next horizon is already being watched.”

role_en: Bring firearm volleys to selected points without surrendering the khanate’s mounted mobility.
lore_en: Mounted musketeers carry guns and powder on horses, dismounting when a stable firing line offers the best effect. They add a direct-fire option against targets that resist arrows while retaining the speed to leave a poor position. Firearms introduce ammunition and maintenance burdens into a riding army. Horse handling and clear orders determine whether the detachment changes roles smoothly or becomes vulnerable between travel and firing.
quote_en: “Ride with the gun. Stand for the shot.”

role_en: Protect the khan and provide selected cavalry for decisive countercharges.
lore_en: The horse guard receives fine mounts, excellent lamellar protection and reliable close weapons. Its riders practise moving around the command group without crowding the wider army’s routes. They can intervene against an exposed threat or exploit a carefully prepared opening. Household loyalty makes them dependable, but high maintenance and limited numbers discourage wasteful pursuit. Guard service requires the patience to remain available while lighter cavalry seeks the first contact.
quote_en: “The khan rides behind a kept promise.”

role_en: Pursue broken troops and win close mounted encounters with experienced sabre riders.
lore_en: Steppe sabre companies carry practical curved blades and protection light enough for sustained riding. Their work begins where a formed opponent loses cohesion, turning disorder into scattered resistance before survivors can rally. They accompany archers and raiders as the close-combat arm of a mobile group. Prepared spear ranks remain dangerous, while pursuit beyond supporting riders can expose the company to fresh infantry or exhausted horses.
quote_en: “The battle ends later for those who run.”

role_en: Complete encirclements and strike decisive exposed sectors with the khanate’s best cavalry.
lore_en: The eternal sky vanguard combines experienced scouts, archery and close striking weapons within selected mounted companies. Its officers judge when pressure from several directions has created a real opening rather than a tempting trap. Excellent horses and disciplined timing allow rapid concentration from a dispersed screen. The unit remains bound by forage and terrain; its elite status improves decisions without granting a horse freedom where the ground denies it.
quote_en: “Close the circle when the opening appears.”

role_en: Reinforce a worthy Great Khan with returned riders carrying the memory and horsemanship of vanished steppe armies.
lore_en: When the Eternal Sky acknowledges a living khan, riders from forgotten hosts may return upon the grass in bodies made whole by Vestigium. They retain the memories, riding skill and battlefield instincts of the warriors they once were, but resurrection grants no immunity: a returned rider can bleed, fall and die like any living man. Their sudden appearance can swell the khanate’s mounted strength without years of recruitment. Those lost after returning cannot simply be called back again during the same manifestation.
quote_en: “Heaven returns the warrior. It does not spare him.”

class_en: Returned Horse Archers · Black Arrow Host
role_en: Overwhelm flanks and marching columns with returned horse archers whose ancestral drill survives intact.
lore_en: The Black Arrow Host gathers returned mounted archers from many generations of steppe warfare. They ride with the instinctive spacing, feigned withdrawals and encirclement discipline learned in lives already spent beneath the open sky. Vestigium restores the warrior and his remembered craft, not an endless supply of bodies or arrows; casualties are permanent within the Host, and sustained battle drains ammunition like any mortal force. Their terror comes from experience repeated across centuries, not from spectral invulnerability.
quote_en: “The dead remember the distance.”

class_en: Returned Household Guard · Great Khan Elite
role_en: Guard the Mandate bearer and deliver disciplined heavy cavalry shock with warriors once sworn to Great Khans.
lore_en: These Kheshig are drawn from household warriors whose oaths once bound them to the greatest rulers of the steppe. Returned in mortal flesh, they bring superb horsemanship, disciplined lance work and an instinctive understanding of protecting a mobile command. Their presence around a recognised Mandate bearer creates a formidable guard and countercharge reserve. Yet even legendary household warriors fall to bullets and cannon; every death permanently thins a formation that cannot be replenished by ordinary recruitment.
quote_en: “We guarded khans before your grandfather knew his name.”

role_en: Transform a moment of recognised Heavenly Mandate into a campaign-scale mounted host capable of breaking an enemy army.
lore_en: At the highest expression of the Mandate, the horizon itself seems to fill with returned riders until tens of thousands of horses move beneath one sky. The Last Horizon is not a permanent army and cannot be recruited, stored or casually redeployed; it appears only when tribal unity, victory and legitimacy align strongly enough for the Eternal Sky to answer. Every warrior manifests in mortal flesh and every casualty is real. The Host exists to decide a campaign, not to garrison cities, replace administration or survive reckless expenditure against prepared guns.
quote_en: “When Heaven remembers, a hundred thousand hooves answer.”

role_en: Maintain saddles, crossings and mobile gun equipment through mounted technical detachments.
lore_en: Mounted engineers pack tools, spare fittings and repair materials across working horses. They keep carriages rolling, reinforce small crossings and restore the tack that sustained movement wears down. Their work supports the khanate’s assumption that every arm can travel quickly. Heavy construction exceeds the loads they can carry, and emergency repairs need protection when the army’s pace leaves a disabled vehicle or tired mount behind.
quote_en: “Speed survives on sound fittings.”

role_en: Move light guns with the riding army to support attacks without fixing the entire force in place.
lore_en: Horse-artillery crews use compact cannon, light carriages and carefully packed stores. Mounted teams shift a battery between firing points, adding shot where bows alone cannot disturb the target. The corps must balance gun weight against the pace of its escort. Limited ammunition and modest calibre restrict prolonged bombardment, while a broken wheel can strand equipment that the rest of the khanate expects to move with it.
quote_en: “The battery rides with the decision.”

role_en: Place legendary steppe commanders beside a living Great Khan when the Eternal Sky judges the Mandate worthy.
lore_en: Attila, Chinggis Khan and other Great Khans are remembered by the grass as more than names. Under rare conditions of unity and recognised Heavenly Mandate, one or more may return in mortal bodies carrying the memory, command instinct and presence of their former lives. They cannot be ordered into existence, and they may refuse an unworthy ruler entirely. Once returned they are flesh and blood: an arrow, musket ball or cannon shot can kill a Great Khan again, making every appearance both a miracle and a terrible risk.
quote_en: “A Great Khan returns only when Heaven has already chosen.”

role_en: Carry horses, riders and light guns across inland rivers and lakes.
lore_en: A broad flat-bottomed barge carries removable horse stalls, ramps and a small gun platform. Sweeps, towlines and shore teams move its awkward weight where riders cannot ford safely. Tribal carpenters repair the hull with ordinary timber and lashings. It is crossing equipment for a horse army, with little value beyond sheltered inland water.
quote_en: “The riders cross with their horses.”

role_en: Provide dependable musket infantry to support the Safavid cavalry’s battlefield manoeuvres.
lore_en: Tofangchi companies give the army a formed firearm arm alongside its prestigious riders. Long guns, powder flasks and regional coats reflect recruitment from several provinces into organised royal service. They occupy firing positions and defend approaches that cavalry alone cannot reliably hold. Maintenance and powder supply remain essential, while a commander who spends all attention on the horsemen can leave effective infantry unsupported at the moment of contact.
quote_en: “The horses turn because this ground is held.”

role_en: Hold palace access and command enclosures with selected shield-and-sabre infantry.
lore_en: Persian sabre guards carry fine curved blades and strong round shields over chosen armour and courtly cloth. Their permanent duties favour close control around entrances where cavalry has little room to work. They stabilise the command group and can counterattack a nearby breach. Their equipment protects a short contest, while limited range and cumbersome armour make exposed advances against settled musketeers a poor use of household expertise.
quote_en: “The inner gate is our battlefield.”

role_en: Watch frontier approaches and guide royal forces through broken border terrain.
lore_en: Kurdish scouts carry practical layered dress, long firearms and compact travel equipment adapted to local routes. Their independent groups observe passes and warn of hostile movement before a royal column enters confined ground. Personal knowledge can outweigh distant maps, giving commanders time to choose a safer approach. Their small strength favours reconnaissance and skirmishing; forcing scouts into a prolonged formed battle consumes difficult-to-replace regional experience.
quote_en: “The pass is quiet for a reason.”

role_en: Deliver tribal lance shock against weakened enemy formations and exposed flanks.
lore_en: Qizilbash lancers retain red headgear, long spears and mounted protection within the Safavid field army. Their fighting strength grows from experienced riders and the cohesion of established households. They are most useful after scouts and missile troops identify a favourable approach. Competing commanders can complicate cooperation, while repeated charges against prepared gunfire waste horses and veterans that the shah cannot quickly replace.
quote_en: “Lower the lance where the line has already bent.”

role_en: Screen Safavid cavalry and harass opponents with flexible mounted archery.
lore_en: Qizilbash horse archers pair composite bows and quivers with practical riding dress and recognisable red headgear. Their groups test hostile formations, watch flanks and withdraw before a costly close engagement. They prepare space for the lancers while preserving a mobile screen. Arrows and forage limit sustained pressure, and differences between household commanders can prevent several capable groups from acting as a coherent field force.
quote_en: “Let the enemy turn before the lancers arrive.”

role_en: Protect the shah and provide professional household cavalry for critical field commitments.
lore_en: Ghulam guards represent the crown’s investment in a corps tied directly to royal service. Fine mail, plate fittings and well-maintained close weapons accompany riders expected to obey common orders across household divisions. They protect command and deliver a selected countercharge when tribal contingents lose cohesion. Their cost and limited strength favour careful employment, while court competition can pull a professional guard toward political duties beyond the battlefield.
quote_en: “The order comes from the shah.”

role_en: Screen royal movements and secure routes through loyalist mounted detachments.
lore_en: Shahsevan riders unite allegiance to the shah with the practical habits of mobile service. Modest protection, carbines or bows and familiar close weapons support escort duty and scouting around the main army. Their groups identify threats before the household guard must intervene. Loyalty helps coordinate a mixed army but does not erase local interests, while demanding long patrols requires a reliable chain of remounts and supply.
quote_en: “The road ahead is part of the oath.”

role_en: Provide veteran cavalry for the shah’s decisive reserve and controlled counterattack.
lore_en: Red-cap veterans retain Qizilbash identity while serving as a selected reserve within royal campaign plans. Excellent mounts and repaired armour reflect years of service, with experienced officers judging when a charge will matter. They recover threatened ground or exploit an enemy already disrupted by missiles. Their value depends on remaining available; prolonged pursuit, factional rivalry and repeated attrition can exhaust a reserve long before its best opportunity arrives.
quote_en: “A veteran waits for a useful charge.”

role_en: Bring light swivel-gun fire to mobile positions using camel-borne artillery teams.
lore_en: Zamburak crews transport small guns on specialised camel saddles, giving Safavid commanders a firearm that can follow mobile forces over difficult routes. Teams manage animals, ammunition and firing positions as a single task. Their shot weight is modest, useful for disturbing troops rather than reducing a fortress. Animal handling and stable aim limit rapid firing, while concentrated counterfire quickly punishes a small and conspicuous crew.
quote_en: “A little gun can reach a distant road.”

role_en: Support royal infantry and cavalry through prepared conventional cannon fire.
lore_en: Safavid field crews organise powder, shot and carriages around selected firing positions. Their guns pressure fixed targets and interrupt enemy concentrations while the horsemen seek an approach. Useful fire depends on maintained equipment and officers who coordinate the battery with the wider plan. Transport remains a burden, and competing household priorities can deny gunners the escort or draft teams necessary to move after the first exchange.
quote_en: “The cavalry needs the opening these guns make.”

class_en: Wardens of the Shah’s Seal · Strategic Custodians
role_en: Transport, secure and contain sensitive relics, documents and dangerous objects entrusted directly to royal authority.
lore_en: Some things within the Safavid state are too politically valuable or too dangerous for ordinary guards. The Wardens accompany sealed royal cargo, maintain hidden repositories and remove compromised material before battlefield disorder can place it in hostile hands. Their loyalty is measured less by ceremonial proximity to the Shah than by whether the seal remains unbroken at the end of the journey.
quote_en: “The seal arrives unopened.”

role_en: Enter enemy rear areas at night to sabotage stores, bridges, communications and selected command targets.
lore_en: Shab-Ravān teams favour darkness, patience and routes ignored by conventional soldiers. They carry light firearms, bows, blades and compact incendiaries, travelling without the banners or baggage that reveal ordinary formations. Their purpose is not to seize ground but to make the enemy wake to missing officers, burning powder and a road that no longer exists.
quote_en: “The camp sleeps once.”

class_en: Armed Gulf Dhow · Patrol and Escort
role_en: Protect local commerce and watch Persian Gulf passages.
lore_en: A regional lateen-rigged hull carries light cannon, water jars and boarding stores. Gulf shipwrights and hired coastal pilots supply practical maritime skills to a court centred on land warfare. This modest patrol craft can discourage small raiders and escort merchants. A true ocean frigate can outgun it, and monsoon weather fixes its operating season.
quote_en: “The gulf keeps its own watch.”

class_en: Gulf Combat Transport · Troop and Convoy Lift
role_en: Move royal detachments while reinforcing local convoy defence.
lore_en: A broader regional sailing hull trades speed for stores, troop benches and a useful defensive battery. Coastal builders strengthen gun beds without adding an expensive ocean battle deck. The shah gains a tool for nearby ports and islands rather than an independent blue-water fleet. Loaded draught and scarce trained gunners limit aggressive operations.
quote_en: “The shore is still within our reach.”

role_en: Provide the empire’s infantry mass and secure local approaches with spear-and-shield musters.
lore_en: Aksumite spear levies gather through local obligations into companies equipped with long points, hide shields and woven layers. They defend approaches and support royal formations, drawing strength from numbers and knowledge of their own district. Their clothing and equipment vary with household resources. Commanders must turn separate musters into a workable line, since courage and familiar terrain cannot alone overcome sustained firearm pressure on exposed ground.
quote_en: “The path to our homes passes through this rank.”

role_en: Hold restricted highland approaches behind substantial shields and disciplined close formations.
lore_en: Highland shield guards carry strong circular hide shields and thrusting weapons with layered woven protection. They are positioned where steep approaches limit the number of attackers reaching the line together. Their defence gains value from chosen ground and supporting missile troops. Shields remain vulnerable to firearms, while cumbersome kit reduces the benefit of chasing a retreat beyond the protected position these infantry were trained to keep.
quote_en: “The slope brings them to our shields.”

role_en: Protect imperial authority and lead selected close engagements with the Negus’s household elite.
lore_en: Royal guards receive fine swords, spears and embellished shields alongside carefully chosen cloth and protection. Their status rests on dependable household service, making them a stable centre around which less permanent musters can rally. The guards defend command and intervene where discipline is essential. Their equipment and experience are scarce; commanders preserve this force rather than scattering it across every local strongpoint or costly frontal attack.
quote_en: “The emperor’s road remains open.”

role_en: Strengthen imperial formations with carefully maintained imported firearm companies.
lore_en: Ethiopian musketeers carry long guns acquired through trade and sustained by local armourers. Woven layers, powder containers and practical belts accompany soldiers whose fire supports shield and spear formations. Different weapon patterns complicate parts and ammunition, making skilled maintenance valuable. These companies are most effective from selected positions with secure supply, while a rapid unsupported exchange can consume the powder reserved for a decisive defensive moment.
quote_en: “One sound lock is worth careful work.”

role_en: Disrupt exposed enemy troops and observe approaches from dispersed highland firing positions.
lore_en: Highland marksmen carry selected long guns with light travel stores and muted woven clothing. They choose observation points and covered routes that allow individual fire without fixing an entire formation. Their familiarity with ground helps identify commanders and exposed crews. Small ammunition stocks and inconsistent firearm quality limit a long exchange. They depend on nearby infantry if an opponent reaches their position in strength.
quote_en: “A clear view is worth the climb.”

role_en: Win close assaults in restricted ground through experienced Tigray sword-and-shield companies.
lore_en: Tigray veterans carry curved shotel blades and strong circular shields with practical woven protection. They close after supporting fire or terrain interrupts the enemy’s formation, using experience to work around shields and confined approaches. Their regional cohesion gives royal officers a dependable assault body. Sword skill remains tied to reaching useful contact; exposed movement under artillery or settled musket fire consumes veterans before their weapons can matter.
quote_en: “Bring the fight within the shield’s reach.”

role_en: Maintain local strongpoints and delay assaults until imperial field forces can respond.
lore_en: Fortress defenders know their stores, entrances and firing positions through permanent service. Spears and shields cover close access while selected guns strengthen approaches vulnerable to direct attack. Their watch routines preserve usable ammunition and warn neighbouring posts of movement. Strong walls do not provide their own food or relief, making a prolonged siege a contest of supply and communication as much as personal courage.
quote_en: “A wall holds longer when the storehouse does.”

role_en: Guard imperial standards and keep local formations gathered around a dependable royal centre.
lore_en: The standard guard combines fine woven dress and selected close weapons with practical battlefield responsibility. Its soldiers protect the recognised rallying point when scattered musters lose contact with orders. Ceremony gives the formation visibility, while experienced officers keep that visibility from becoming a needless exposure. Their work requires steadfast defence and clear signals; losing the guard can unravel cohesion well beyond the number of men immediately engaged.
quote_en: “Find the standard. Find the line.”

role_en: Secure Red Sea landings and protect imperial coastal stores with compact naval infantry.
lore_en: Red Sea marines adapt shield, blade and firearm equipment to boats, quays and narrow harbour approaches. Their detachments escort stores and hold the landing point through which inland troops must pass. Regional seamanship and compact loads distinguish them from highland musters. Their strength is local maritime access, while long inland service removes nearby boats and coastal supply without giving them the weight of the royal guard.
quote_en: “The shore is the first gate inland.”

role_en: Observe routes and pursue scattered opponents with compact highland cavalry detachments.
lore_en: Mountain cavalry uses smaller loads and practical riding arms to remain useful around difficult approaches. Spears, shields and selected firearms support reconnaissance and escort work rather than repeated massed shock. Riders identify routes, gather reports and reach exposed detachments ahead of foot troops. Horses still require forage and suitable footing, making steep confined ground a reason to dismount or withdraw rather than a challenge elite riders can simply ignore.
quote_en: “The horse takes the route it can survive.”

role_en: Provide limited cannon support against fixed targets and threatened imperial approaches.
lore_en: Imperial field gunners serve a small number of valuable pieces acquired and maintained through specialist labour. Simple carriages, prepared powder and deliberate target selection make every battery a strategic commitment. The guns can interrupt a concentrated attack or pressure a fortified point. Draft teams, ammunition and repair parts restrict their deployment, so royal commanders place them where a few useful shots can influence the wider infantry battle.
quote_en: “Choose the target before spending the powder.”

role_en: Pursue anomalies and hostile specialists across cliffs, escarpments and mountain routes beyond ordinary military access.
lore_en: The Dega Asashoch treat altitude as protection rather than hardship. Small teams climb routes that artillery cannot follow and cavalry cannot survive, searching caves, abandoned monasteries and isolated highland sites for threats reported by local communities. Their strength is not supernatural power but the ability to reach places where supernatural threats expect no army to arrive.
quote_en: “There is always another path upward.”

role_en: Fight and secure tunnels, rock-cut structures, mountain vaults and confined strongpoints inaccessible to conventional formations.
lore_en: Aksum’s revived empire inherits landscapes in which stone itself has been shaped into sanctuary, fortress and passage. The Vault Wardens train for combat inside narrow stairs, carved galleries and underground chambers where numbers become useless and one disciplined defender can stop many. They also guard repositories that imperial authorities prefer outsiders never discover.
quote_en: “Stone remembers who belongs beneath it.”

class_en: Armed Red Sea Dhow · Coastal Patrol
role_en: Escort local traders and secure approaches to Massawa.
lore_en: A manageable lateen sail and light gun battery suit the narrow channels around the port. Coastal pilots supply the maritime knowledge imperial highland officers lack. Short voyages keep repairs and freshwater within reach. The hull can resist ordinary raiders, but strong winds and ocean warships expose its limited protection.
quote_en: “The mountain’s stores arrive by sea.”

class_en: Red Sea Escort Transport · Trade Protection
role_en: Carry troops and supplies beside escorted Red Sea commerce.
lore_en: A broad regional hull carries cargo below a defended deck and uses a second sail for loaded passages. Island anchorages around Dahlak support water, pilots and repairs. The vessel ties coastal commerce to imperial troop movement. Heavy loading slows its response, and its modest battery relies on company rather than fleet combat.
quote_en: “Guard the passage and the highlands eat.”

role_en: Supply broad provincial missile support through massed Kongo archery.
lore_en: Kongo bow levies muster with bows, quivers and woven clothing supplied through their districts. Their numbers allow broad screens of arrows and flexible support around stronger shield companies. Local officers keep the groups together and know how to replenish familiar equipment. The levy system produces uneven readiness, while bows lose effectiveness against heavy protection and sustained gunfire. Royal plans therefore depend on coordinating many provincial contributions rather than assuming identical regiments.
quote_en: “Every district sends its arrows.”

role_en: Protect close approaches and support attacking infantry with noble shield-bearing companies.
lore_en: Adargueiros carry substantial shields and well-made swords, often drawing on imported metalwork alongside local equipment. Their status supplies better protection and training than ordinary musters, creating a valuable centre for close infantry action. They move with archers and gun companies that prepare the approach. Shield-bearing nobles are limited in number, and their protection does little to justify crossing exposed ground under concentrated artillery.
quote_en: “The shield is carried where the arrows end.”

role_en: Lead close infantry commitments with experienced nobles and excellent sword equipment.
lore_en: Kongo fidalgos bring household followers and regional authority into the federation’s army. Fine woven dress and imported blades mark status, but useful leadership depends on keeping companies coordinated when separate chiefs bring their own troops. They fight near decisive entrances and contested command points. Prestige can steady a muster or encourage rivalry, making royal officers responsible for aligning ambition with a common military objective.
quote_en: “A title must stand where its followers can see.”

role_en: Provide selected firearm support through royal musketeers supplied from central stores.
lore_en: Royal Kongo musketeers carry imported guns and maintain powder equipment under more consistent supervision than provincial levies. Their companies deliver short, useful volleys alongside the army’s archers and shield infantry. Central support helps keep valuable firearms serviceable, while mixed models and scarce replacement parts complicate maintenance. Commanders place them where clear targets justify ammunition, preserving gunpowder for moments when it can change the enemy’s confidence or formation.
quote_en: “Keep the lock sound and the shot useful.”

role_en: Stabilise provincial infantry lines through experienced Mbamba companies.
lore_en: Mbamba veterans carry repaired spears, shields and regional cloth that records practical service rather than common imperial tailoring. Their experience helps less seasoned musters keep intervals, protect missile troops and respond to local pressure. They provide cohesion without requiring every province to adopt the same equipment. Commanders must still coordinate separate leaders and supply routes, while long attrition removes the seasoned core on which a much larger contingent depends.
quote_en: “The younger ranks watch our feet.”

role_en: Find hostile movement and guide federation columns through difficult forest approaches.
lore_en: Kongo forest scouts travel in small groups with light bows, spears and practical cutting tools. Their knowledge of paths and settlement routes warns commanders before large musters become trapped in narrow ground. They choose observation and ambush positions for supporting infantry. Their strengths depend on local contacts and freedom to move, with little armour or ammunition for a direct contest against formed troops.
quote_en: “The next clearing is already watched.”

role_en: Reinforce the federation’s infantry mass with allied Ngola spear companies.
lore_en: Ngola allied spears retain their own textiles, shields and leaders while contributing close infantry to shared campaigns. Familiar drill keeps each contingent useful around defended approaches and beside missile troops. Their inclusion widens the federation’s manpower without creating a uniform central army. Cooperation depends on clear objectives and respected obligations, while distant supply or rivalry between chiefs can reduce the number of troops available when orders arrive.
quote_en: “We came for the agreed ground.”

role_en: Preserve battlefield communication and rallying points through protected drum detachments.
lore_en: Royal drum guards carry close weapons around the players whose signals keep dispersed contingents linked to command. Familiar rhythms transmit changes of pace and calls to gather when shouted orders disappear. The detachment protects both instruments and interpreters, giving the federation a practical means of coordination. Signals lose meaning when companies lack common training, while conspicuous sound and position draw enemy attention toward a valuable command link.
quote_en: “Listen for the order your chief knows.”

role_en: Secure ferry points and move small detachments across the federation’s waterways.
lore_en: River guards organise paddles, compact spears and shields around boats used for transfer and local defence. They watch crossing points, escort stores and create the first foothold for a larger contingent. Knowledge of channels and banks can save a column days of difficult travel. Their transported loads remain small, and a defended landing can pin lightly equipped troops before the rest of the force reaches the far bank.
quote_en: “Hold the bank until the next boat.”

role_en: Provide a selected common reserve drawn from the federation’s strongest household troops.
lore_en: The household guard brings experienced soldiers from several kingdoms into a formation entrusted with shared command protection. Excellent shields and blades accompany distinctive regional cloth, preserving identities within agreed campaign discipline. The guard can rally a mixed line or counterattack a threatened entrance. Its creation depends on cooperation among rulers, and its limited strength makes every casualty a loss of both military experience and political trust.
quote_en: “Many households. One guarded command.”

role_en: Smash weakened formations, terrify militia and serve as a rare prestige shock arm for royal commitments.
lore_en: Horse culture remains limited in much of Kongo’s environment, so the federation’s most memorable mounted terror comes from elsewhere. Rhinoceros Riders are rare, difficult to maintain and never fielded in large numbers, but when released under noble supervision, their sheer mass and intimidation can shatter less steady enemies. More than a routine cavalry arm, they are a symbol of royal audacity and a weapon of concentrated shock.
quote_en: “Not every beast was born to flee from kings.”

role_en: Strengthen selected defensive positions with a limited pool of imported field cannon.
lore_en: Kongo gunners serve valuable pieces with carefully stored powder and locally maintained wooden fittings. Their batteries support defended approaches rather than following every provincial muster into the field. Imported patterns and small specialist crews make maintenance a significant commitment. Cannon can disturb a concentrated attack, but the federation’s army must still fight chiefly through its infantry when roads, draft teams or ammunition prevent a battery from reaching the chosen ground.
quote_en: “The gun guards one approach. The army guards the rest.”

class_en: Leopard Path Hunters · Deep Forest Strike Teams
role_en: Track hostile leaders, raiders and monsters through dense forest before guiding a concentrated ambush.
lore_en: The Leopard Path Hunters work in groups small enough to disappear beneath the forest canopy. Their campaigns are measured in tracks read, camps found and targets isolated rather than ground occupied. Spears, bows and firearms vary by region, but concealment and patience remain constant.
quote_en: “The leopard does not require an army.”

role_en: Identify dangerous spiritual or Vestigium disturbances, protect sacred objects and advise commanders when ordinary military solutions may worsen a crisis.
lore_en: The Banganga serving the federation are respected specialists rather than battlefield sorcerers. Their knowledge of medicines, ritual practice, community memory and sacred objects helps commanders distinguish between panic, disease, fraud and genuine anomalous danger. When Vestigium phenomena appear, they work beside soldiers to isolate the affected place and prevent outsiders from turning local belief into another weapon.
quote_en: “Power is dangerous when nobody remembers its name.”

class_en: Great River War Canoe · Crossing Control
role_en: Move federal troops and command fighting on navigable river reaches.
lore_en: A long dugout core with raised plank sides supports many paddlers and a small protected command platform. One light imported cannon adds firepower without changing the river hull into a sailing ship. Provincial crews bring local current knowledge. Rapids, low sides and recoil limit where the federation can commit it safely.
quote_en: “The kingdoms cross together.”

role_en: Hold port gates and protect the stores through which the league’s maritime strength is sustained.
lore_en: Swahili port guards carry spears, blades and selected firearms in layered coastal dress. Their watches connect harbour access, warehouses and nearby streets into a defensible settlement. Merchant support keeps vital posts equipped, while local officers know how people and cargo normally move through the port. Their strength is fixed familiarity; a distant inland campaign demands transport and field organisation beyond the duties for which these garrisons were assembled.
quote_en: “The harbour begins at this gate.”

role_en: Support defended shore approaches with patient matchlock fire from protected positions.
lore_en: Coastal matchlock companies draw powder and maintenance from port stores, firing across approaches measured during regular watches. Long cotton layers and simple flasks suit familiar duties around walls and landing grounds. Their old mechanisms can still deliver useful volleys when the position protects slow loading. Salt, damp and inconsistent supplies require care, making prolonged unsupported movement far inland much less forgiving than service beside a maintained harbour magazine.
quote_en: “The wall gives time to light the match.”

role_en: Protect Zanzibar’s household authority and counterattack nearby threats with selected guards.
lore_en: Zanzibar guards combine fine coastal textiles, strong shields and well-made blades with permanent household discipline. They defend entrances and command groups where recognisable authority helps separate an organised response from a panicked crowd. Selected equipment and training make them valuable in short close engagements. Their limited numbers and royal obligations restrict distant deployment, leaving the league’s broad defence to port garrisons and maritime troops.
quote_en: “The inner court has heard the alarm.”

role_en: Escort merchant stores and defend caravan access connecting Kilwa’s port to its inland trade.
lore_en: Kilwa merchant guards carry practical firearms and blades with loads suited to escort work. Their duties include watching baggage, managing defensible halts and keeping valuable goods moving through crowded transfer points. They know the routes and contacts on which a commercial expedition depends. Guard contracts cannot create unlimited field strength, so these detachments avoid chasing raiders far enough to leave the caravan and its supplies unprotected.
quote_en: “The cargo reaches the gate together.”

role_en: Maintain coral-built strongpoints and keep harbour defences functioning through a siege.
lore_en: Coral-fort defenders know the passages, wells and stores behind their walls. Spears and shields cover close access while selected firearms support the gunners. Their duties include repairing damage and maintaining a watch when bombardment interrupts ordinary routines. Fortification gives a small force endurance, but relief and water remain decisive. A strong post can become isolated if the league loses the boats and roads that sustain it.
quote_en: “The wall needs hands after every shot.”

role_en: Secure shore routes and reinforce landing defences with allied spear infantry.
lore_en: East African spear auxiliaries retain distinct regional textiles and local command relationships within the league’s defence. Spears and hide shields suit road junctions, stores and nearby landing grounds where maritime troops need a dependable infantry screen. Their contribution extends the ports’ reach into surrounding territory. Commanders gain strength through clear obligations and local supply, while distant expeditions make these lightly equipped contingents harder to sustain.
quote_en: “The port stands because its roads are held.”

role_en: Seize hostile decks and secure landing stages through trained dhow boarding detachments.
lore_en: Dhow marines keep firearms and blades compact enough for movement around rigging and crowded rails. Weatherproof powder storage and practiced boat handling support the first contact, after which disciplined groups protect access for following crews. Their experience turns a merchant fleet into a means of armed action. Open inland fighting removes the confined approaches and nearby vessels that help these lightly protected troops control an engagement.
quote_en: “Keep a place for the next boat.”

role_en: Conduct fast coastal raids against exposed vessels, stores and lightly defended landing points.
lore_en: Sailor raiders carry boarding blades and short firearms with the practical loads of working crews. They use maritime access to choose a brief contest, seize an objective and leave before heavier defenders gather. Their operations pressure a coastline without requiring possession of a large inland territory. An alert fortified port or rough weather can defeat the approach, while remaining too long ashore exposes the limited strength behind a rapid raid.
quote_en: “Take what the next tide can carry.”

role_en: Guide maritime movements and warn commanders of unsafe approaches through experienced navigation.
lore_en: Navigator detachments carry sounding lines, charts and practical instruments beside compact personal weapons. Their knowledge of currents, shoals and seasonal sailing patterns keeps transports from arriving at the wrong coast or grounding under hostile guns. They work with boat scouts and port watches rather than seeking direct combat. Losing an experienced guide can strand an expedition whose soldiers remain perfectly ready to fight but have nowhere safe to land.
quote_en: “A safe passage is part of the victory.”

role_en: Provide a seasoned marine reserve for contested harbours and difficult landing operations.
lore_en: Maritime veterans combine practiced musket handling with seamanship and close boarding work. Repaired but excellent equipment records repeated service across the league’s ports, where detachments must cooperate with crews and local garrisons. They stabilise the first foothold or recover a threatened quay. Their strength is scarce experience and clear coordination, while long inland deployment consumes the maritime reserve the league needs to keep its sea lanes defensible.
quote_en: “We have held this shore in worse weather.”

role_en: Escort merchants and commanders, provide mobile musket fire and imitate inland cavalry methods where prestige or necessity demands it.
lore_en: The Swahili city-states are not true horse powers, yet fashion, rivalry and military imitation still produce small mounted gun units in coastal service. These riders are useful as escorts and mobile skirmishers, but their horses, doctrine and training seldom match the more established cavalry cultures inland. They exist partly for practicality and partly because no ambitious port wishes to look provincial beside its rivals.
quote_en: “We ride because the world expects riders.”

role_en: Deny hostile naval approaches with heavy guns served from prepared Mombasa positions.
lore_en: Mombasa gunners maintain coastal pieces whose firing arcs command selected harbour entrances. Crews organise shot, powder and repair fittings around strong defensive works, aiming to disrupt an approach before troops land. Nearby stores support sustained service but also become critical targets. Fixed cannon cannot cover every inlet, making infantry reserves and warning boats necessary when an opponent seeks a shore outside the prepared arcs.
quote_en: “Turn the ship before it reaches the anchorage.”

role_en: Breach coastal fortifications, harbour gates and coral-built defensive structures during raids and sieges.
lore_en: Swahili ports understand the strengths of coral architecture better than most attackers, and therefore also understand where it fails. These compact sapper teams study mortar lines, sea gates, foundations and powder placement to turn local architectural knowledge into precise demolition. Their work allows a small maritime force to open a defence that would otherwise demand a prolonged siege.
quote_en: “We built these walls. We know where they break.”

role_en: Infiltrate defended harbours by water to sabotage vessels, chains, rudders, moorings and coastal infrastructure.
lore_en: The League’s most unusual specialists begin operations beneath the waterline. Night Divers approach by small boat or swim from beyond harbour watch, carrying compact tools and charges protected against seawater. A fleet may awaken intact yet unable to sail because steering cables are cut, anchors fouled and the harbour chain has mysteriously failed.
quote_en: “The sea has doors no wall can guard.”

role_en: Keep coastal merchant passages open against small raiders.
lore_en: A lean regional dhow carries conventional light guns without sacrificing monsoon handling. Port merchants share maintenance costs while experienced pilots choose seasonal routes and anchorages. Its strength comes from reliable escort presence and local knowledge. Thin sides and a small magazine discourage exchanges with heavy foreign frigates.
quote_en: “The cargo has a guardian.”

role_en: Carry valuable loads while organising long seasonal convoys.
lore_en: A broad planked hull accommodates cargo, freshwater and a defensive deck battery. Two large regional sails carry it between league ports as monsoon winds permit. Merchant captains fund guards and navigators who know the ocean’s seasonal demands. Heavy loading reduces speed, and every extra gun displaces paying freight.
quote_en: “The season carries the city’s wealth.”

role_en: Intercept light craft and land raiding parties through reef channels.
lore_en: An enlarged local outrigger canoe carries a small fighting platform and light swivel piece. Stabilising floats help its crew manage a light sail close to reef-fringed shores. Paddles finish quiet approaches before boarding. The platform remains vulnerable to surf and heavy recoil, keeping raids short and carefully timed.
quote_en: “The reef opens for a light keel.”

role_en: Guard harbour chains and cover vulnerable landing approaches.
lore_en: A broad shallow local hull carries a reinforced forward gun bed and several sweeps. Shore arsenals keep its ammunition close while pilots choose prepared firing positions. This economical craft gives coral ports a mobile battery within sheltered water. Low freeboard and slow handling make offshore service dangerous.
quote_en: “The harbour has another wall.”

role_en: Move league detachments and stores between threatened coastal ports.
lore_en: A roomy regional hull carries removable benches, awnings and landing equipment above secured provisions. Its small battery protects loading rather than seeks a duel. Coastal crews time arrivals with tides so troops step ashore as organised detachments. Overcrowding and scarce water limit the distance of an expedition.
quote_en: “The next port will hold.”

role_en: Carry stores through shallow coastal reaches and support dispersed ports.
lore_en: This league adaptation retains the mtepe’s distinctive sewn-plank tradition, projecting prow and woven mat sail. Its flexible hull serves coastal carriage and shallow anchorages. Light swivels sit on reinforced platforms, with heavy guns deliberately excluded. Lashings need regular care, and war loads must respect the construction’s limits.
quote_en: “A league is carried by its smaller ports.”

role_en: Defend settlements and reinforce local posts through armed citizen musters.
lore_en: Cape citizen militia brings personal firearms, practical coats and varying field experience into local defence. Familiar roads and nearby stores allow a modest republic to gather useful strength quickly when alarms spread. Officers assign clear posts rather than expecting identical professional regiments. The muster loses effectiveness when service drags far from homes and livelihoods, while ammunition and uneven training limit its ability to sustain a long conventional campaign.
quote_en: “The alarm reaches every door.”

role_en: Hold the republic’s essential garrisons with salaried infantry and dependable musket drill.
lore_en: Republic line guards supply continuity between temporary musters. Maintained uniforms, common firearms and regular watches keep magazines, harbour entrances and command posts secure when citizens return to their livelihoods. They can form a steady centre for a larger defensive force. Their numbers remain modest, forcing officers to choose which positions need professionals and which can be entrusted to local militia without weakening the republic’s reserve.
quote_en: “Someone stays after the muster ends.”

role_en: Observe frontier movement and guide republican forces through local routes.
lore_en: Khoikhoi allied scouts contribute tracking and route knowledge to the republic’s defence. Practical clothing and light weapons suit observation ahead of heavier detachments, identifying water, crossings and concealed movement. Their experience deserves clear authority within reconnaissance plans rather than being treated as incidental support. Small groups remain vulnerable if fixed in direct combat, so commanders protect the intelligence network by using reports before the scouts must fight.
quote_en: “The tracks tell us where the patrol went.”

role_en: Disrupt exposed enemy leaders and crews with selected long-gun marksmen.
